severity.Catastrophic: Death or permanent disabling injury to any person; fire not contained to the unit; lithium-ion cell venting with flame or explosion. Register safety dimension 5.
severity.Critical: Injury requiring medical treatment (second-degree burn, permanent hearing threshold shift); fire or smoke contained to the unit; RF exposure of the operator above the 47 CFR 1.1310(b) occupational limit, or of a bystander, guest or household member above the 47 CFR 1.1310(c) general-population limit; harmful interference to a radionavigation or other safety service (47 CFR 97.3(a)(23)). Register safety dimension 4.
severity.Marginal: First-aid injury (minor burn or cut, temporary hearing discomfort recovering within 24 h); destruction of the unit without fire; RF exposure of the operator above 50 percent of the 1.1310(b) occupational limit or of a bystander above 50 percent of the general-population limit; interference to another amateur station or a Part 97 emission violation without a safety-service victim. Register safety dimension 3 (first aid) or 2 (discomfort).
severity.Negligible: Discomfort or nuisance without injury: an audible click, a warm surface below 45 C, cosmetic damage, a birdie in the receiver. Register safety dimension 1.

likelihood.A: Frequent: expected every time the initiating condition occurs, more than once per unit-year, or inherent to normal operation without the control.
likelihood.B: Probable: expected several times in the fleet life (at most 5 units, about 15 unit-years); a single common operator error or a single common component fault (contact bounce, a mono plug, an undeburred edge) is enough.
likelihood.C: Occasional: expected about once in the fleet life; needs an uncommon operator action or a single component or firmware fault.
likelihood.D: Remote: not expected in the fleet life but credible; needs a rare fault, or one fault plus an uncommon condition.
likelihood.E: Improbable: needs two or more independent faults, or a fault plus a deliberate defeat of a control; assumed not to occur in the fleet life.

response.High: Unacceptable as a residual. A design change or an additional independent control is required before PDR; a hazard still High at PDR is a Major RID (01 section 10.2) and a hazard without an allocated control requirement can never be a lien from PDR onward (01 section 12.2).
response.Serious: Acceptable as a residual only with owner acceptance recorded in a decision memo, at least two independent controls of which one is neither software nor procedure, and verification of every control by Test.
response.Medium: Acceptable as a residual with the listed controls allocated to requirements and verified, and the owner's acceptance recorded at SAR; Claude manages; listed at every review.
response.Low: Acceptable; controls documented, allocated and verified by the method assigned in the requirement; listed at every review.

hazards.title: RF exposure of the operator in the portable posture (SAR within 20 cm)
hazards.description: The operator holds the radio with the whip within 20 cm of the head, hand or torso while transmitting up to 5 W (6.3 W at the +1 dB step tolerance with ALC; up to 10 W at 8.4 V full drive if the ALC is absent or failed) at 144 to 148 MHz. Within 20 cm the portable-device SAR regime of 47 CFR 2.1093 applies and, because every operator is a licensee (SI-030), the 1.1310(b) occupational limits govern: 8 W/kg over any 1 g, 20 W/kg over any 10 g of an extremity, averaged over 6 minutes with duty-factor averaging permitted. No SAR measurement path exists at project scale; exposure is estimated by analogy to FCC equipment-authorization SAR values of commercial VHF handhelds (0.05 to 0.35 W/kg per W at 50 percent duty, six radios).

causes.cause: Long key-down or a continuous tune carrier with the antenna at the face; a continuous carrier is the only case above the 40 percent conversational-CW duty factor.
Output power above the selected step: ALC absent or failed, full-charge droop giving 6.4 to 10 W at 8.4 V.
Power step reverts to 5 W after a configuration reset, or the tune carrier does not time out.
A higher-gain (5/8 wave, +2 dBd) or a stubby antenna substituted; smaller antennas raise the local SAR for the same power.

Stuck key (HZ-004): a continuous carrier is bounded to 13 s by the hardware cutoff; a toggling key stream (a held paddle lever, a squeeze from headphones or a shorted TRS cable inserted after boot) is bounded by firmware only, and indefinitely if firmware also fails, until the HZ-004 K12 backstop exists.

hazards.effects: Under the high analogy value (0.35 W/kg per W at 50 percent duty) the licensee's 1 g SAR is 17.5 percent of the 8 W/kg limit at 5 W continuous CW and 43.8 percent for a 6 minute continuous 5 W carrier; the limit is reached only at 28.6 W continuous CW or 11.4 W continuous carrier. Exceeding the occupational limit therefore needs an over-power fault (a 10 W carrier at the face reaches 87.5 percent) together with a continuous carrier beyond the timeouts. If exceeded: tissue heating above the limit's safety margin and a regulatory non-compliance for the licensee; no acute injury at these levels.
hazards.rationale: Severity Marginal: the worst credible uncontrolled case (a 10 W carrier at the face for 6 minutes) is 87.5 percent of the occupational SAR limit, so the harm is loss of the limit's margin, not an injury. Likelihood C: a continuous tune carrier with the radio held at the face is an uncommon but foreseeable operator action; the over-power condition additionally needs a fault. Confidence Medium-Low on the absolute SAR numbers (docs/research/rf-exposure-evaluation.md F6): the analogy spread is 7:1 and the homebrew aluminum enclosure with an end-mounted whip weakens the FCC 'strong similarity' condition, which is why the hazard is carried at Medium rather than Low. Exposure of the operator above the 1.1310(b) limit is Critical on the section 3.2 scale; under the high analogy value it is not reached even in the uncontrolled worst case (87.5 percent), so the hazard stays Marginal; if the RF exposure evaluation (RFX-18) or RSK-030 shows that the limit can be exceeded, the severity rises to Critical.

firmware_role.statement: Firmware controls when RF exists (keying and PA enable), the selected power step, its default and the deliberate action to select 5 W, and the tune-carrier level and timeout (criterion b); the key-down timeouts that bound duty provide mitigation (criterion c). The 6 min and 30 min key-down accumulator and the on-screen separation reminder are convenience functions, not safety-critical (owner decision RFX-D4 pending).
components: PA enable and TX sequencer (power step, tune timeout, TX permit)

controls.text: Operator-selectable output steps 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 W, each within +/-1 dB into 50 ohm; default 1 W at first boot and after any configuration reset; the selected step persists thereafter; selecting 5 W requires a deliberate action distinct from tuning and volume (SWE-134 d). Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (RFX-D1, RFX-D2).

Tune carrier at the 0.5 W step by default, ending automatically 5 s +/-0.5 s after it starts (proposed), which keeps it below the 7.5 s floor of the hardware cutoff so that the cutoff never ends a legitimate tune; raising the tune level is a deliberate action. REQ-SYS-020 now bounds every tune carrier to at most 5.5 s (TBR) after it starts, 2 s below the 7.5 s floor of REQ-SYS-055, which removes the conflict of the research value (10 s +/-1 s could be cut by every unit whose T_max is below 11 s). Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (package decision 36, RFX-D3 together with D-KN2; OQ-SAF-005).

tbr.item: 5 s tune timeout (RFX-D3 and D-KN2 consistency)
tbr.owner: Claude proposes; Robin decides at SRR
tbr.plan: Robin chooses at SRR (package decision 36) between (a) a 5 s +/-0.5 s tune timeout, recommended; (b) a T_max floor above 11 s with the 13 s thermal and exposure bounds re-derived; (c) a tune carrier that drops TX_KEY periodically, not recommended because it removes the hardware bound from the tune carrier. The RF exposure evaluation and the PA thermal analysis confirm the value at PDR.

controls.note: REQ-SYS-020 reads at most 5.5 s (TBR) since 2026-09-25, consistent with REQ-SYS-055; the value closes with package decision 36 (OQ-SAF-005).

controls.text: The firmware stuck-key controls of HZ-004 (manual-closure timeout 5 s, K3; no-gap paddle watchdog with squeeze limit, K4) end an unintended key-down or key stream before it adds material duty.

Closed-loop ALC (gate-bias loop with a forward-power detector) holds the selected step within +/-0.5 dB from 6.4 to 8.4 V, so the full-charge output cannot exceed the 5 W step by more than 0.5 dB; the exposure evaluation carries the ALC-off 10 W case as the fault bound.

Operations handbook RF exposure section: the two tiers and who is in each, the time-averaged power, MPE distance and SAR tables of the evaluation updated with measured power and antenna gain, the operating rules, the antenna gain envelope (not above 0 dBd; a higher-gain antenna requires re-evaluation), and a one-page station-evaluation form; this is the information the occupational tier requires (47 CFR 1.1310(e)(2), 97.13(c)(1)).

ConOps nominal posture: radio on a surface or in the hand at waist level with the antenna base 20 cm or more from head and torso (mobile posture, closed by the MPE analysis); handheld-at-face is the off-nominal scenario evaluated by SAR analogy; an optional external antenna on a short coax moves the unit into the mobile regime (RFX-D5). Carried into the handbook as REQ-SYS-122 checklist item 'HZ-001 K6'; REQ-SYS-123 usability runs are supporting validation only.

Permanent enclosure legend (CNC-engraved or laser-marked): amateur radio transmitter, 144 to 148 MHz, 5 W maximum, for use by licensed amateur operators, RF exposure information in the named handbook section (RFX-D9).

RF Exposure Evaluation as a controlled document produced at PDR from the OET 65 Supplement B recipe and the SAR analogy, updated at CDR with the chosen antenna and at TRR with measured power per step and the whip's EIRP relative to a reference dipole (KX4O method, tinySA Ultra); it states which conclusions rest on the analogy and its caveats (RFX-18).

The independent hardware PA-enable cutoff of HZ-004 K5 bounds any continuous key-down to 13 s, so a 100 percent duty carrier cannot persist through the 6 minute averaging window. It does not bound a toggling key stream, which only K10 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180) bounds in hardware; even an unbounded 5 W carrier at the face stays at 43.8 percent of the occupational limit under the high analogy.

The transmission-length backstop of HZ-004 K12 (REQ-SYS-180) ends antenna-port RF, independently of firmware, after 180 s (TBR) of continuous transmit, so a toggling key stream that retriggers the K9 cutoff on every edge cannot hold the carrier duty beyond 180 s without a second fault. Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (package decision 38); if the owner declines, REQ-SYS-180 is retired by the SRR decision memo and this control becomes Dropped.

residual_risk.condition: K1 to K4 verified; the RF exposure evaluation accepted by the owner (RFX-D6) with the analogy validity carried as an accepted risk in the register. Exceeding the occupational limit then needs an ALC fault, a carrier beyond every timeout and the radio at the face together.

hazards.verification_note: K1, K2: HostUnit tests of step selection, default, persistence, confirmation logic and the tune timeout on the injected clock as the closing Test (SWE-192); Bench power per step into the dummy load at 6.0, 7.4 and 8.4 V with the tinySA Ultra and a calibrated attenuator, and the tune duration by logic capture. K3, K9, K10: as HZ-004 K3, K4, K5 and K12. K4: Simulation (behavioural PA model) then Bench. K5, K6, K7: Inspection against the RF exposure evaluation, the ConOps, the REQ-SYS-122 handbook checklist and the rendered enclosure legend. K8: Inspection at PDR, CDR and TRR. The SAR figure itself closes by the Analysis method (REQ-SYS-121, accepted per RSK-016) with Simulation-class evidence (the OET 65 Supplement B recipe and the SAR analogy in a checked calculation); no Test exists at project scale.
hazards.fault_tolerance: Zero-fault tolerant by margin for the operator tier: the exposure stays below the occupational limit with every listed control absent, provided the antenna gain is at or below 0 dBd and power is at or below 10 W. The controls keep the margin under a single over-power fault and bound the duty: a continuous carrier by hardware at 13 s, a toggling key stream by firmware, and by hardware through K10 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180) once package decision 38 adopts it.

hazards.title: Lithium-ion cell overcharge or charging fault leading to venting or thermal runaway
hazards.description: The 2S pack of user-replaceable 18650 cells (SI-023) is charged from the Pico 2 micro-USB (SI-022) by an on-board 2S boost charger. A charging fault that drives either cell above 4.25 V, charges below 0 C or above 45 C, exceeds the charge current, continues past a safe time, or charges a reversed, mismatched or damaged cell can cause lithium plating, an internal short, venting and thermal runaway inside a sealed aluminum enclosure that is held in the hand or carried in a pocket.

causes.cause: Charger IC regulation fault (VREG or battery OVP failure, wrong PSEL strap or register state) applies more than 4.25 V to a cell.
Cell imbalance beyond the balancing capability, so one cell exceeds 4.25 V while the pack voltage reads normal.
Charging with the cell below 0 C or above 45 C because the thermistor is not thermally coupled to the cell or the JEITA thresholds are misconfigured.
Firmware writes a wrong charge profile or ignores a charger fault flag.
USB source over-voltage (a bad adapter) beyond the charger input rating.
Mixed-age, mismatched or damaged cells inserted, or a cell reversed; the holders do not prevent reversed insertion.
Runaway charge time: termination is never reached because the receiver load masks the termination current.
Heat from the PA raises the cell temperature when charging follows a long transmission.

hazards.effects: Cell venting with flame inside the enclosure, fire, burn injury, smoke and destruction of the unit; the Pico 2 datasheet caution applies: bare, unprotected cells can catch fire or explode if over-charged or charged outside their allowed temperature and current range. Register safety dimension 5.
hazards.rationale: Severity Catastrophic: lithium-ion venting with flame is the register's safety level 5 and this analysis's Catastrophic definition. Likelihood B in the uncontrolled state: inserting mixed-age, mismatched or reversed cells (C6) is a single common operator error by any of the several users who replace the cells (SI-019, SI-023), which is the B anchor of section 3.3; with the charger IC as the only regulator one IC fault or one misconfiguration is also enough, and protected cells cannot be assumed because they do not fit 65 mm holders. Re-rated from C to B after independent review. Confidence Medium (datasheet thresholds are High confidence; thermistor coupling and holder behaviour are Low).

firmware_role.statement: Firmware supervises the charger over I2C, compares the charger ADC against the RP2350 divider readings and disables charging on disagreement or fault (criterion c); it detects the fault, reports it on the LCD and takes the corrective action (criterion e). Firmware cannot raise the charge voltage above the charger IC's hardware limit and is not in the primary protection path.

controls.text: Charger IC (TI BQ25887 class): 2S CC-CV to 4.20 V +/-0.5 percent per cell with battery OVP, JEITA temperature window from a cell-mounted 10 kohm NTC (no charge below 0 C or above 45 C at full rate, suspend above 60 C), 12 h safety timer, VBUS OVP 6.2 to 6.6 V, input current limit 500 mA by default (D-PWR-01).

Independent 2S protection IC (ABLIC S-8252 class) with a dual N-channel FET in the pack negative lead opens the charge path at 4.25 V +/-0.02 V per cell and on charge over-current (-0.100 V sense), with internal delay timers and quiescent current below 10 uA (D-PWR-03).

Secondary 2S over-voltage protector (TI BQ29209 class) opening the charge path at 4.30 V (TBR) per cell with 15 mA balancing, as a third layer independent of the charger, the 4.25 V protector and firmware, on its own cell sense connections (K9) (D-PWR-03, recommended yes). No requirement implements it: REQ-SYS-083 is the 4.25 V protector (K2), and its rationale allocates this layer to the power subsystem at PDR; the L1 requirement is requested in OQ-SAF-008.
controls.note: Does not count toward the residual until its requirement exists (section 3.5).

controls.text: Dual dissimilar sensing: each cell voltage read through the charger ADC over I2C and through an RP2350 ADC divider; charging inhibited and the fault shown on the LCD when the two disagree by more than 100 mV or the charger reports a fault; the RP2350 path is calibrated against the charger ADC at each USB connection. A disagreement is a latched cell-sensing fault (ConOps Table 3.4-4 row 13) whose safe state disables charging first (REQ-SYS-130).

tbr.plan: Set from the calibration analysis of the RP2350 ADC path (30 mV reference offset, 0.9 percent gain error) at PDR.

controls.text: Insertion check: charging refused and a warning shown when the cells differ by more than 300 mV at insertion or either cell reads outside 2.5 to 4.3 V; 'no cells' reported when the charger sees no battery; a charge-state watchdog stops and reports charging that exceeds 12 h or shows no current fall. A reversed, out-of-window or mismatched cell and a charger fault are latched faults (ConOps Table 3.4-4 rows 14 and 15) whose safe state disables charging first (REQ-SYS-130).

tbr.plan: Set at PDR from the charger's balancing capability and the chosen cell's tolerance.

controls.text: Cell NTC mounted against the cell body inside the holder (not a board-temperature sensor); charging paused while the receiver runs so termination is not masked (D-PWR-07, recommended default); charger cell balancing to 400 mA above 3.7 V per cell.

Cells retained in their holders, separated from the PA thermal zone by distance or a barrier, enclosure vent path with no sealed cavity around the cells, no sharp edges near the cells (RSK-007 S4). REQ-SYS-099 (a firmware 60 C lock-out) does not implement this design property; the requirement or a recorded ME allocation with PDR closure is requested in OQ-SAF-010.

Handbook: approved cells (one brand and age, unprotected INR18650 class, or protected cells only if they fit), polarity, do not charge after a fault indication, do not charge unattended overnight, storage state of charge.

Separate Kelvin sense connections: each protection layer (charger cell sensing and balancing, the 4.25 V protector, the 4.30 V secondary protector and the firmware dividers) takes its own sense trace from each cell terminal at the holder tab, with its own series resistor, so that one open or high-resistance sense connection blinds at most one layer. The current proposal shares one MID sense net (300 ohm, HZ-007 K3) among all layers. Requirement pending (OQ-SAF-009).

residual_risk.condition: With the allocated controls (charger regulation K1, 4.25 V protector K2, firmware dual sensing and insertion check K4 and K5) an overcharge needs two independent device failures, except through the shared MID sense net: one open or high-resistance MID sense connection plus a cell imbalance (common with mixed cells, C6) blinds the per-cell detection of every layer while the charger holds the pack at 8.4 V, which is one fault plus a common condition (D, Low confidence: the firmware disagreement check may catch a floating MID input). Serious needs the owner's acceptance in a decision memo (section 3.4). With K3 (OQ-SAF-008) and the Kelvin sense constraint K9 (OQ-SAF-009) allocated and verified by Test with a bench supply substituting for each cell, an overcharge needs three independent devices on independent sense paths to fail and the residual becomes Catastrophic-E, Medium, accepted by the owner at SAR under the RSK-007 acceptance record.

hazards.verification_note: K1, K2, K3: Inspection of the register map and thresholds against the datasheets before power-on; Bench with a bench supply substituting for each cell as the closing Test: charger VREG and termination, protector over-voltage trip and release, secondary protector trip, JEITA behaviour with the NTC heated and cooled. K4, K5: HostUnit fault-injection tests as the closing Test (SWE-192) and Bench. K6, K7, K9: Inspection of the layout, the sense routing and the enclosure model, plus a Bench thermal measurement of cell temperature during a charge that follows a 5 minute key-down; K9 also Bench, one sense connection opened at a time with a bench supply per cell, each layer confirmed to trip on its own. K8: Inspection of the handbook.
single_point_failures: Shared MID sense net and holder junction (300 ohm series, HZ-007 K3): the charger, the 4.25 V protector, the 4.30 V secondary protector and the firmware dividers all sense the cell junction through one net, so one open or high-resistance sense connection blinds per-cell over-voltage detection in every layer; removed as a single point only by the K9 Kelvin sense constraint (requirement pending, OQ-SAF-009)

Cell NTC decoupled from the cell: charger JEITA and firmware lock-out then both read board temperature; mitigated by placement design and a bench thermal check, single point for the temperature window
The cells themselves (counterfeit, damaged or mismatched cells are outside the design's control): user guidance and the insertion check only
hazards.fault_tolerance: Overcharge: single-fault tolerant with the allocated controls (charger regulation and the 4.25 V protector are independent devices), with the shared MID sense net as a named single point for per-cell detection; two-fault tolerant only when the 4.30 V secondary protector K3 has its requirement and each layer has its own Kelvin sense route K9, both requirement pending until the PDR allocation. Temperature window: single-fault tolerant (charger JEITA and the firmware lock-out share one NTC, a named single point).

hazards.title: Power amplifier and enclosure over-temperature and contact burn
hazards.description: The 5 W PA dissipates about 4 to 7 W (the two-stage RD07MUS2B line-up draws 11.4 W DC at 5 W out; the RA07M1317M module dissipates 7.9 W at 6.5 W out) inside a pocket-sized aluminum enclosure whose wall is the heat sink and is held in the hand. Sustained keying (the pack supports about 1.5 h of continuous key-down at 5 W), a blocked or insufficient heat path (RSK-006), a bias or ALC fault, high SWR or a stuck key raises the PA junction and the enclosure surface temperature.

causes.cause: Long transmission or tune carrier at 5 W in a hand or a pocket.
Thermal path (filled vias, pad, standoff or gap pad to the wall) insufficient for the dissipation (RSK-006).
PA gate-bias fault raising dissipation, or ALC fault giving 8.5 to 10 W output at full charge.
Thermal fold-back or inhibit does not act: sensor reading cold, wrong threshold, stalled monitor task.
Hot ambient, radio in a pocket or in the sun, heat path blocked by the hand.
High SWR, open or shorted antenna port raising device dissipation (device load ruggedness 20:1 VSWR at rated power).

hazards.effects: Enclosure hand-hold surface above the touch limit for metal held for long periods (project proposal 48 C, TBR). With the radio in a pocket or against the skin during long or stuck 5 W keying (causes C1, C3, C5; the pack supports about 1.5 h of continuous key-down at 4 to 7 W PA dissipation in a small aluminum case), the skin-contact surface can stay above about 55 C for minutes, which produces a partial-thickness (second-degree) contact burn; the PA junction can pass 150 C, with device failure and smoke contained to the unit; heat conducted to the cells (HZ-007 C5). Register safety dimension 4.
hazards.rationale: Severity Critical: the uncontrolled state includes long or stuck 5 W keying with the radio in a pocket for up to the 1.5 h the pack supports, which can hold the skin-contact surface above about 55 C for minutes (a partial-thickness burn needing medical treatment) and drive the junction past 150 C (device failure with smoke contained to the unit); both are Critical on the section 3.2 scale. The earlier Marginal rating stopped at first aid and was corrected after independent review. Likelihood C: RSK-006 rates an insufficient thermal path at likelihood 3 (a single analysis pending); long keying is common but a hazardous surface temperature needs the design shortfall or a fault in addition. Confidence Medium-Low: the burn threshold figures are general burn-injury data not in the corpus, and the PDR thermal budget does not yet exist.

firmware_role.statement: Firmware sets the PA bias and power, a function identified in the hazard (criterion b), and reads the PA thermistor, folds back power, inhibits transmit and recovers with hysteresis (criterion e).

controls.text: PA thermal path designed for continuous key-down at the 5 W step in 40 C ambient with the junction at or below 110 C (REQ-SYS-112, TBR), and for the hand-hold surface at or below 48 C after 5 minutes of continuous key-down at 5 W in 25 C ambient (REQ-SYS-113, TBR): Type VII filled vias under the PA, a thermal interface from the PCB thermal area to the enclosure wall, fit-checked on an H2C print.

tbr.item: 48 C surface limit and 110 C junction limit
tbr.plan: Fixed by the PDR thermal budget (RSK-006 S1); the surface figure is the touch-temperature value commonly used in consumer product safety standards for metal held for long periods; that standard is not in the corpus, so the number is a project proposal until then; numbers aligned with REQ-SYS-112 and REQ-SYS-113.

controls.text: PA thermistor sampled at 20 Hz with range and plausibility checks; power fold-back above a threshold and transmit inhibit within 100 ms above a limit (85 C TBR), recovery with hysteresis, fault shown on the LCD (SWE-134 g, j).

tbr.item: 85 C inhibit threshold and fold-back threshold
tbr.owner: Claude prepares the PA thermal analysis; Robin decides
tbr.plan: The PDR thermal analysis fixes both thresholds; the values are written into the L2 SW requirement and the ADR.

controls.text: The firmware stuck-key controls of HZ-004 (manual-closure timeout 5 s, K3; no-gap paddle watchdog with squeeze limit, K4) end an unintended key-down or key stream.

ALC caps the output at the selected step within +/-0.5 dB from 6.4 to 8.4 V, so dissipation does not rise with pack voltage; every element after the PA is rated for the full-charge, full-drive output unless the ALC is shown to limit power under all single faults.

PA device with load ruggedness of at least 20:1 VSWR at rated power; the transmitter delivers rated power at SWR up to 2:1 and survives 60 s of continuous key-down into any load up to 10:1 at any phase and into open and short circuits; optional forward and reverse power detector with fold-back above SWR 3:1 (antenna DECISION-5, PDR).
Handbook states the continuous key-down behaviour, the PA temperature warning on the LCD and the fold-back, and advises against transmitting with the radio in a pocket.

Thermal budget at PDR (dissipation at 50 percent key-down duty and a 5 minute continuous worst case, resistance chain junction to enclosure); Bench 5 minute key-down into the dummy load inside the enclosure with the NTC logged over serial and the surface temperature read with the multimeter thermocouple (RSK-006 S1, S4).

The hardware PA-enable cutoff of HZ-004 K5 bounds a continuous carrier to 13 s. It does not bound normal long keying or a toggling key stream: K10 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180) bounds a stream to 180 s TBR, inside the 5 minute thermal design case, and only K9 (REQ-SYS-181) bounds normal long keying independently of firmware.

Hardware over-temperature cut-off independent of firmware: a thermal fuse or PTC on the PA supply, or a comparator on a second NTC at the PA that forces the PA-path enable low above a fixed threshold (95 C TBR at the sensor) with hysteresis. Brought forward from PDR as an SRR decision (recommended adopt); without it the thermistor-failure branch has no independent control. Implemented by REQ-SYS-181 (Hardware PA over-temperature cut-off, Draft, 95 C TBR; OQ-SAF-012). Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (package decision 39); if the owner declines, REQ-SYS-181 is retired by the SRR decision memo and this control becomes Dropped.

hazards.title: Unintended or stuck transmission
hazards.description: The transmitter is keyed without the operator's intent or stays keyed after the intent has ended: a mono (TS) plug grounding the ring contact; headphones or another device in the key jack (a 32 ohm load reads as a closed contact: a closure at power-on, a continuous closure in Straight mode, and a squeeze on both contacts in the iambic modes, which produces an endless alternating dit-dah stream); a stuck or dirty key or paddle contact; an iambic keyer state fault (dit or dah memory never cleared); a keyer task stall; a latched TX_KEY or PA_EN output; an undefined pad state after reset or in the bootloader; a corrupted keying state; a bench test-mode keying stream left running; or a pin-map error driving TX_KEY with a periodic output. The keyer and the PA-enable path are the only paths that key the transmitter for both key types (SI-018). A continuous key-down and a toggling key stream are different fault classes: the hardware cutoff K5 bounds only the first.

causes.cause: A mono (TS) plug grounds the ring contact (documented by the Elecraft KX3 straight-key note and the QRP Labs QCX and QMX manuals).

Headphones or another low-impedance device plugged into the key jack: read as a closed contact at power-on (interlock), as a continuous closure after boot in Straight mode, and as both paddle contacts closed (a squeeze giving an endless alternating dit-dah stream) after boot in Iambic A (the default), Iambic B or Ultimatic mode.
Stuck, dirty or bouncing key or paddle contact, a stuck paddle lever (a stream of identical elements), or a shorted TRS cable closing both contacts after boot (a squeeze stream in the iambic modes).
Iambic engine fault (a dit or dah memory never cleared, giving an endless toggling element stream), sequencer fault holding TX_KEY, timeouts misconfigured.
Firmware hung or a task stalled with TX_KEY high.

PA_EN or TX_KEY pad undriven after reset or in the bootloader (pads reset to input-disabled with a weak 36 to 113 kohm internal pull-down) and read as high by the PA logic without an external pull-down.
Memory corruption of the keying or permit state (SWE-134 f).
RF pickup or ESD on the key line read as a closure (HZ-010).

Bench test-mode keying stream (the PARIS string into the dummy load, a continuous carrier; docs/conops/conops.md section 3.5.2 item 2) left running, entered by a fault or persisted across a reset; a PARIS loop has 7-dit word spaces, so neither a gap-based watchdog nor the retriggerable hardware cutoff sees it.

Pin-map or PWM-slice configuration error in a release driving TX_KEY (and PA_EN) with a periodic output (HZ-014 C5): the retriggerable cutoff is restarted by every edge and a firmware watchdog that stops keying through SIO cannot override a wrong pad function.

hazards.effects: Continuous carrier at up to 5 W (10 W at full charge without ALC): RF exposure at 100 percent duty (HZ-001, HZ-006), PA heating (HZ-003), an unidentified carrier occupying a frequency (47 CFR 97.101(d), 97.119), battery depletion; the operator may not notice with the headphones off. Worst credible: a 5 W carrier for 30 minutes in a guest's hands exceeds the general-population SAR limit (HZ-006), and the carrier causes harmful interference to another service on the frequency.
hazards.rationale: Severity Critical because the worst credible outcome is the HZ-006 exceedance for a guest and harmful interference (47 CFR 97.3(a)(23)) to another service. Likelihood B in the uncontrolled state: the mono-plug trap is documented by two vendors, stuck contacts are common, friends' keys arrive with unknown plugs (SI-019, SI-034), and headphones in the key jack in the default Iambic A mode give a squeeze stream. Confidence High for the architecture of the continuous-key-down controls (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F13), Medium for the monostable timing spread, Medium for the toggling-stream controls, which were added after independent review and are not in F13.

firmware_role.statement: A keyer or sequencer fault causes or contributes to the hazard from either key type (criterion a); the keyer and the PA-enable gate control the keying function identified in the hazard (criterion b); the interlock, timeouts, the no-gap watchdog on the TX_KEY read-back (run by the safe-state manager, independently of the keyer engine), the test-mode guard and the safe state provide mitigation (criterion c). The keyer commands the hazardous operation (SWE-134 note).

controls.text: Power-on and reset interlock: transmit arming requires both key inputs confirmed open for at least 500 ms after boot and after every reset; otherwise transmit is inhibited, the sidetone is off, the LCD shows 'KEY CLOSED: check plug' and the check repeats every sample (SWE-134 a, h).

Straight-on-tip mode is selected only by an explicit menu action after the interlock has passed, never by automatic detection; the ring contact is then ignored, which makes a mono plug safe (SWE-134 d). Mode changes only by menu (D-KN8).

Manual-closure timeout T_sw = 5 s (configurable 2 to 6 s, always below the hardware cutoff minimum of 7.5 s): any manually timed continuous closure (Straight mode and the Bug-mode dah contact) confirmed for longer than T_sw drops TX_KEY through the normal envelope fall, keeps the sidetone on so the operator hears the fault, shows 'KEY?' and re-arms when the contact is confirmed open (SWE-134 j; D-KN3). REQ-SYS-053 covers 'any continuous manually timed key closure', the Bug-mode dah contact included (OQ-SAF-004 closed); the 5 s value is its TBR (package decision 37).

No-gap paddle watchdog, run by the safe-state manager on the TX_KEY read-back and not by the keyer engine, so that a keyer fault that produces a stream does not also disable it: keying stops, with the sidetone continuing and an alert shown, when (i) 128 consecutive identical elements are sent; (ii) TX_KEY has had no key-up interval of at least 7 dit times at the selected speed or 500 ms, whichever is shorter, for 30 s, whatever the element pattern; or (iii) both paddle contacts have stayed closed for more than 2 s in Iambic A, Iambic B or Ultimatic mode (a squeeze from headphones or a shorted TRS cable inserted after boot). Items (ii) and (iii) redefine REQ-SYS-054, which today counts identical elements only (OQ-SAF-001, OQ-SAF-002). Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (package decision 37, D-KN3).

tbr.item: No-gap interval (7 dit times or 500 ms) and 30 s window
tbr.plan: Checked at PDR against HostUnit replays of recorded normal sending at 5, 15, 25 and 50 WPM (no trip) and against every stream case of the hazard-analysis.md section 5 coverage table (trip); written into REQ-SYS-054.
Checked against the longest squeezed character at 5 WPM (C, 11 dit times, 2.64 s): if normal squeezing trips it, the limit becomes the longer of 2 s and 16 dit times; decided with REQ-SYS-054 at PDR.

controls.note: REQ-SYS-054 covers item (i) only; items (ii) and (iii) requested in OQ-SAF-001 and OQ-SAF-002 (package decision 37). With K12 a stream that K4 misses is still ended in hardware at 180 s (TBR).

controls.text: Independent hardware PA-enable cutoff: a retriggerable monostable (Nexperia 74LVC1G123 class, 1 Mohm, 10 uF) watches TX_KEY; each key-down edge starts a pulse of T_max = 10 s nominal (acceptance 7.5 to 13 s); the PA path is enabled only while TX_KEY AND Q are both true, so a TX_KEY that stays high longer than T_max from any cause loses the PA until the line falls and rises again; the cutoff acts on the envelope modulator control node, not on the LDMOS gate bias alone (SWE-134 i; D-KN2). Because every TX_KEY edge restarts the pulse, K5 bounds a continuous key-down only; a toggling TX_KEY stream retriggers it indefinitely (K12). The T_max value, its window and the 74LVC1G123 part are Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (D-KN2, package decision 36).

tbr.item: T_max window 7.5 to 13 s and the cutoff node
tbr.plan: Window confirmed from the 74LVC1G123 K factor versus VCC and the 10 uF capacitor DC-bias derating; cutoff node confirmed against the PA topology chosen at PDR (R-KN5).

controls.text: TX_KEY and PA_EN carry external 4.7 kohm pull-downs (inside the RP2350-E9 '8.2 kohm or less' guidance) so that reset, bootloader and isolated pad states read low at the PA logic; the T/R relay's unpowered state connects the antenna to the receiver (TR-04).

CPU watchdog of at most 2 s enabled before transmit can be armed; the reset reason is recorded; every reset, panic or fault path enters the safe state (PA off, key up, audio muted) before anything else (SWE-134 a, c, l).

Two independent software conditions for RF: a keyer key-down event and a separately maintained PA-permit flag from the safe-state manager, both refreshed periodically; the keying and permit state is stored with its bitwise complement and checked before every use (SWE-134 f, i).

Key inputs sampled at 1 kHz and debounced (closure accepted after 2 consecutive 1 ms samples, opening after 5, fixed counts that are not operator-configurable per REQ-SW-KEYER-020 and 021, TBR; the fixed-count choice is an owner decision at SRR) with stuck-input detection; the HZ-010 network attenuates RF pickup by about 70 dB before the Schmitt hysteresis (SWE-134 g). Key-down is withheld while a key input reads closed with no plug present (REQ-SW-KEYER-036).

tbr.item: Debounce 2 ms make and 5 ms open
tbr.plan: Closed by the bench capture of the owner's key and paddle bounce (A-KN5, TC-KEY-BOUNCE) before PDR, because REQ-SYS-048 is an L1 requirement and L1 TBRs close by PDR (charter section 7).

controls.text: Key jack wiring fixed in ICD-CTL-KEY (tip = dit or hand key, ring = dah, sleeve = ground); handbook one-line plug check and the meaning of the KEY CLOSED message (R-KN3).

The operator can unplug the key or paddle and can remove the PA supply with the mechanical power switch (D-PWR-08); the stuck-key abort is REQ-SYS-122 checklist item 'HZ-004 K11' in the handbook and is written into every bench procedure (hazard-analysis.md section 10); MOE-008 usability runs (TC-VAL; REQ-SYS-123 is retired) are supporting validation only.

Transmission-length backstop independent of firmware: a second monostable watches the T/R transmit drive and removes the PA-path enable at the same node as K5 when the drive has stayed in transmit continuously for 180 s (TBR), re-arming only when the drive returns to receive (hang time expired); proposed with it, the PA-path gate also requires the T/R transmit drive, so a TX_KEY stream with T/R in receive gives no PA output (confirmed at PDR). It is the only hardware element that bounds a toggling TX_KEY stream (hazard-analysis.md section 5, coverage rows 4 to 8). Brought forward from PDR to SRR for the owner's decision (package decision 38). Alternatives rejected: a leaky-integrator duty limiter on TX_KEY misses continuous dits (50 percent duty) and a PARIS loop (44 percent); a cutoff that re-arms only after a minimum TX_KEY low time cannot serve 5 to 50 WPM, because the 240 ms intra-character gap at 5 WPM is longer than the 168 ms word space at 50 WPM. Implemented by REQ-SYS-180 (Transmission-length hardware backstop, Draft, 180 s TBR; OQ-SAF-003), shared as HZ-001 K10, HZ-003 K10, HZ-006 K10, HZ-012 K6 and HZ-014 K8. Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR; if the owner declines, REQ-SYS-180 is retired by the SRR decision memo and this control becomes Dropped.

tbr.owner: Claude proposes; Robin decides at SRR
tbr.plan: Set at SRR against the longest legitimate over without a pause longer than the hang time (up to 2500 ms, REQ-SYS-044); confirmed at PDR by timing Simulation of the monostable over tolerance; kept above the 120 s bench test-mode timeout (K13) so that firmware acts first.

controls.text: Bench test modes (full-scale tone, PARIS string into the dummy load, continuous carrier under the tune limits, watchdog demonstration; ConOps section 3.5.2 item 2): entry only by a menu action plus a confirmation (SWE-134 d; REQ-SYS-007 covers the confirmed entry for keying), the transmitter forced to the 0.5 W step, automatic exit after 120 s (TBR) and on every reset, never persisted in the configuration store, and a 'TEST' indication for the whole mode. A PARIS loop has 7-dit word spaces, so K4 does not see it and K5 is retriggered; K13 and K12 are its controls. Requirement pending for the forced step, the timeout, the reset exit and the non-persistence (OQ-SAF-016; package decision 41); REQ-SYS-179 implements the menu-plus-confirmation entry.

tbr.plan: Set at PDR from the longest bench measurement a test mode must support (element timing at 5 WPM, about 60 s) and kept below the K12 backstop.

residual_risk.condition: Critical-D, Medium, with every control that has a requirement verified, the transmission-length backstop K12 (REQ-SYS-180, Proposed, package decision 38) included: a toggling key stream from a single cause (headphones or a shorted TRS cable inserted after boot in Iambic A, a held paddle lever, an iambic memory fault, a test-mode PARIS loop, a release with a periodic output on TX_KEY) is ended by K12 after 180 s (TBR) of continuous transmit even when firmware K4 cannot act, so a longer transmission needs a firmware fault plus a backstop failure, and a continuous carrier longer than 13 s needs a firmware fault plus a cutoff failure (both E). The level is set by the shorted envelope pass element single point (R-KN5), which bypasses K5 and K12 alike, and becomes Critical-E, Low, once R-KN5 closes at PDR. K4 items (ii) and (iii) and the K13 forced step, timeout, reset exit and non-persistence are requirement pending (OQ-SAF-001, OQ-SAF-002, OQ-SAF-016; package decisions 37 and 41) and do not count (section 3.5). If the owner declines package decision 38, REQ-SYS-180 is retired by the SRR decision memo, K12 becomes Dropped and the residual reverts to Critical-C, Serious, set by coverage rows 4 to 8 of hazard-analysis.md section 5, which then have only software (K4, K13) and operator procedure (K11) controls. Section 3.4 accepts a Serious residual only with the owner's acceptance in a decision memo, at least two independent controls of which one is neither software nor procedure, and every control verified by Test; the toggling-stream branch fails the second condition, so the decline cannot be accepted as a residual: the SRR decision memo records it as a decision the section 3.4 response does not allow and names the alternative hardware control or design change, with its requirement, to be allocated before PDR (OQ-SAF-003).

hazards.verification_note: K1 to K4, K7 to K9, K13: HostUnit tests with golden vectors, fault injection and the injected clock as the closing Test (SWE-192, no exception for software controls), including every stream case of the hazard-analysis.md section 5 coverage table (single lever held, both contacts closed after boot in each iambic mode, a keyer-memory fault that alternates elements, a PARIS loop in test mode) and replays of recorded normal sending that must not trip K4; Emulation scenarios for event ordering only (ACC-EMU-001 scope); Bench logic capture of TX_KEY and PA_EN with the PA disconnected (stage 6 of the power-on sequence). K5, K12: Simulation of the monostable timing windows including capacitor DC-bias derating; Bench as the closing Test: a fault-injection build holds TX_KEY high (K5), or holds the T/R drive in transmit while toggling TX_KEY (K12), with the PA disconnected, and the logic capture times the PA-path enable; repeated at every unit's ATP. K6: Inspection of the schematic; Bench at power-on stages 4 and 6 (bootloader and reset states read low). K10, K11: Inspection of ICD-CTL-KEY and of the handbook against the REQ-SYS-122 checklist; Bench demonstration of the abort actions.
single_point_failures: Hardware cutoff timing capacitor (10 uF ceramic with DC-bias derating): a value loss shortens T_max; with the tune carrier of REQ-SYS-020 (at most 5.5 s, TBR; OQ-SAF-005) the margin to the 7.5 s floor is 2 s and a further loss interrupts legitimate tune carriers and long manual key-downs (nuisance, R-KN1); an open capacitor lengthens T_max toward indefinite, a latent loss of the backstop detected only by the Bench timing test at TRR and each ATP

Envelope modulator pass element shorted (PA fed regardless of the control node): the cutoff K5, the backstop K12 and the ALC all lose authority because they act on that node; single point unless the cutoff also removes gate bias or a second series element is added (PDR decision R-KN5)

Without K12, no hardware element bounds a toggling TX_KEY stream (a held paddle lever, a squeeze from headphones or a shorted TRS cable inserted after boot in an iambic mode, an iambic memory fault, a bench test-mode PARIS loop, a periodic output on TX_KEY from a pin-map error): K5 is retriggered by every edge, so firmware K4 and K13 are the only automatic controls and a pin-map error can defeat both; removed by K12 (REQ-SYS-180) if the owner adopts package decision 38; stays a single point if declined (OQ-SAF-003)
hazards.fault_tolerance: Continuous key-down (TX_KEY held high from any cause): single-fault tolerant with dissimilar controls (firmware timeout K3 or watchdog K4, hardware monostable K5, reset-safe pad states K6): no single software fault sustains a continuous carrier beyond 13 s. Toggling TX_KEY stream: zero-fault tolerant in hardware, because K5 is retriggered by every edge; bounded only by firmware K4 and the test-mode guard K13, which a pin-map error can defeat; single-fault tolerant once the transmission-length backstop K12 (REQ-SYS-180, package decision 38) is adopted and verified. SWE-134 i (no single software event initiates the hazard) holds for initiation through the two software conditions K8; it holds for sustaining a toggling stream only with K12.
decisions_pending: D-KN2 (package decision 36): adopt the hardware cutoff with T_max 10 s; 74LVC1G123 (recommended) versus LTC6993-2; the 7.5 s floor must stay above the tune timeout, REQ-SYS-020 at most 5.5 s (OQ-SAF-005)

D-KN3 (package decision 37): firmware manual-closure timeout 5 s (including the Bug-mode dah contact) and the no-gap paddle watchdog with squeeze limit (128 identical elements; 30 s without a key-up interval of 7 dit times or 500 ms; both contacts closed over 2 s)
D-KN8 (package decision 44): mono plug handled by interlock plus menu, no automatic mode change, for rev A

Package decision 38 (SRR, brought forward from PDR): transmission-length backstop K12 on the T/R drive, REQ-SYS-180, 180 s TBR (recommended adopt); a decline leaves the toggling-stream branch at Critical-C, Serious, which section 3.4 does not accept with firmware as the only automatic control
Package decision 41 (SRR): bench test-mode guard K13 (menu plus confirmation, forced 0.5 W, 120 s timeout, exit on reset, never persisted)
R-KN5: cutoff node versus PA topology (bias-only cutoff may not silence a driven LDMOS)

hazards.title: Hearing damage from headphone level, full-scale tones and clicks
hazards.description: Headphones of 16 to 64 ohm (earbud sensitivities measured up to 121.6 dB/V) are driven by the audio amplifier. An unrestricted amplifier (TPA6132A2 class, 22 mW into 32 ohm, 0.84 Vrms) produces 113 to 120 dB SPL and the other candidates up to 126 dB SPL; a firmware fault (a full-scale PWM pattern at start-up, sidetone at maximum, AGC off with a strong signal), a component failure in the level-setting network, or a T/R or turn-on click delivers this to the ear.

causes.cause: Amplifier full-scale output far above safe listening levels with no fixed attenuation.
Full-scale PWM pattern at start-up or after a fault, corrupted volume state, limiter bypassed, sidetone gain at maximum.
Strong signal (a nearby 5 W station) with AGC off and no limiter.
DC step or amplifier turn-on pop at T/R transitions, plug insertion or power-on (acoustic startle).
Failure of a level-setting component: the shunt element of the output divider open raises the output to the amplifier's full scale.
Bench test-mode full-scale 700 Hz tone (docs/conops/conops.md section 3.5.2 item 2) selected, left running or entered by a fault while headphones are on the ear.

hazards.effects: Acoustic shock or noise-induced hearing injury: 113 to 126 dB SPL exceeds the 118 dB(A) steady-state acoustic-shock ceiling used for telephony headsets (ITU-T P.360) and is 13 to 26 dB above the 100 dB(A) consumer maximum of EN 50332 and IEC 62368-1 clause 10.6; a permanent threshold shift is an injury requiring medical treatment. Register safety dimension 4.
hazards.rationale: Severity Critical: a permanent hearing threshold shift from a full-scale tone at the ear is an injury requiring medical treatment. Likelihood B uncontrolled: a firmware start-up full-scale pattern or a maximum-volume setting is a single common fault or a single operator action, and every amplifier candidate can produce the level. Confidence High for the amplifier and norm figures (docs/research/audio-output-and-hearing-safety.md F19 to F25), Medium for earbud sensitivities (secondary measurements).

firmware_role.statement: Firmware controls the audio output level identified in the hazard (criterion b); the sample-domain limiter, the default cap, the ramps and the fault mute provide mitigation (criterion c). The hardware ceiling bounds any firmware fault.

controls.text: Hardware output ceiling: headphone output into 32 ohm not above 150 mVrms for any digital output pattern and 100 mVrms +/-10 percent for a full-scale 700 Hz sine, set by fixed passive components and fixed amplifier gain, independent of firmware state (bounds 96.5 dB SPL for EN 50332-2 boundary phones and 101.6 dB SPL for the most sensitive earbuds measured).

Default level cap 30 mVrms-equivalent (about 85 dB(A) class) until the operator acknowledges a high-level warning by a menu action plus a confirmation (SWE-134 d); the unlocked cap is the hardware ceiling; the acknowledgment expires after 20 h of cumulative unlocked operation and reverts at power-on unless persisted by explicit choice (audio D2 option a).

Sample-domain limiter with attack at or below 1 ms bounding receive audio and sidetone to the active cap, including with AGC off; sidetone and receive audio are mixed before the limiter; volume ramped at or below 1 dB per ms. REQ-SYS-072 and REQ-SYS-074 set the bounds the limiter enforces; no requirement states the 1 ms attack time (OQ-SAF-015).

Receive audio faded to -60 dBFS or below with a raised-cosine ramp within 2 ms of key-down, held muted through transmit and the hang interval, restored with a 5 to 20 ms fade; sidetone onset within 1 ms of key-down with a 3 to 5 ms envelope; no DC step at any transition; synthesizer driver writes that do not reset the PLL while tuning.

Amplifier enable pulled down in hardware and asserted by firmware only after the audio source has idled at mid-scale for at least 20 ms and the coupling capacitors have charged; de-asserted on brown-out or fault; amplifier with click-and-pop suppression and output short-circuit protection; 80 dB input-to-output attenuation in shutdown.

Tip-switch jack detection (Same Sky SJ1-3535N class switched jack): the amplifier is shut down with no headphones and the LCD indicates it; on insertion the output ramps from zero over 100 ms after a 50 ms debounce.

The passive ceiling network is arranged so that no single component failure raises the output above 150 mVrms: the series element open fails silent and the shunt element is redundant or its open failure is bounded; confirmed by single-failure Analysis at PDR.
Handbook states the level policy, the unlock and its expiry, the recommendation to use headphones of 16 ohm or more, and that a full-scale test tone exists only in the bench test mode.

Full-scale test tone only in the bench test mode: entry by a menu action plus a confirmation, automatic exit after 60 s (TBR) and on every reset, never persisted; the hardware ceiling K1 still bounds it to 100 mVrms; the bench rule of hazard-analysis.md section 10 keeps headphones off the ear during the tone. Requirement pending (OQ-SAF-016).

residual_risk.condition: Hardware ceiling verified on the bench with a 32 ohm load and the single-failure analysis accepted. With the ceiling in place the worst case is 105 dB SPL (150 mV into the most sensitive earbuds measured) for the duration of a fault, a temporary discomfort at the consumer maximum.

hazards.verification_note: K1, K7: Simulation (LTspice of the divider, reconstruction and coupling network with a behavioural amplifier model, including single-component-failure cases) and Bench (AC RMS across a 32 ohm 1 percent load with the firmware full-scale 700 Hz test tone and the worst-case square-wave pattern; the multimeter's AC accuracy at 700 Hz confirmed from its manual first); REQ-SYS-073 closes by the Analysis method accepted per RSK-017. K2 to K4, K9: HostUnit with synthetic tone bursts asserting peak, attack time and DC step, and the test-mode entry and exit rules, as the closing Test (SWE-192); Bench RMS check of the 30 mV cap and a listening check of the fades; REQ-SYS-076 closes by the Analysis method accepted per RSK-017 (no oscilloscope for the 10 mV transient bound). K5, K6: Inspection of the schematic and Bench (turn-on pop measured, insertion ramp observed). K8: Inspection.

hazards.fault_tolerance: Single-fault tolerant: the hardware ceiling bounds any firmware fault; the firmware cap and limiter bound normal operation below the ceiling; no single component failure may defeat the ceiling (K7).

hazards.title: RF exposure of bystanders, household members and non-licensee holders (general population)
hazards.description: Persons other than the operating licensee are evaluated at the general-population limits: 47 CFR 1.1310(c) SAR 1.6 W/kg over any 1 g, 4 W/kg over any 10 g of an extremity, averaged over 30 minutes with source-based averaging only (2.1093(d)(4)); MPE 0.2 mW/cm2 at 30 to 300 MHz (1.1310(e)(1) Table 1). Two exposures: (a) a bystander 20 cm or more from the antenna (MPE regime); (b) an unlicensed guest who holds and keys the unit as a third party under supervision (47 CFR 97.115(b)(1)) or who picks up a unit at a gathering (SI-019) with the whip within 20 cm (SAR regime). A licensee's household members may be evaluated at the occupational tier only if they have accessed the exposure information (97.13(c)(1)).

causes.cause: A guest keys the unit at the 2 W or 5 W step, or runs a tune carrier, with the whip at the face.
A bystander closer than 0.6 m to the antenna during keying or closer than 1.0 m during a 5 W tune carrier (0 dBd whip, 2.56 reflection factor).
A unit loaned or handed over with 5 W selected and no receive-only lock.
A higher-gain antenna (+2 dBd 5/8 wave) grows the bystander distances to 0.73 m (CW) and 1.16 m (carrier).
Several cwht units operating in one place: fractional contributions add for a bystander in the same 30 minute window (47 CFR 1.1307(b)(3)(ii)(B)).
A stuck carrier (HZ-004) removes the source-based duty-factor averaging; a toggling key stream at a guest's face is bounded by firmware only until the HZ-004 K12 backstop exists.

hazards.effects: Under the high analogy value a 5 W continuous carrier at the face of a non-licensee is 219 percent of the general-population 1 g SAR limit (106 percent at the median value), 5 W continuous CW 87.5 percent; the 2 W step gives 87.5 percent (carrier) and 35 percent (CW); 1 W gives 43.8 and 17.5 percent; 0.5 W gives 21.9 and 8.7 percent. Bystander MPE compliance distances (0 dBd, 2.56 reflection): 0.58 m at 5 W continuous CW, 0.91 m during a 5 W carrier, 0.26 m at 1 W CW. Exceeding the general-population limit is the register's safety level 4.
hazards.rationale: Severity Critical: exposure of a non-licensee above the 1.1310(c) limit is the register's Major (4) safety level and this analysis's Critical definition; the limit's own safety factor means no acute injury is expected at twice the limit, but the analysis treats an exceedance as the credible harm. Likelihood C uncontrolled: guest keying at a gathering is the foreseeable misuse that SI-019 creates; reaching the exceedance additionally needs the tune function or a long key-down at the face. Confidence Medium-Low on the SAR numbers (7:1 analogy spread), High on the MPE distances.

firmware_role.statement: Firmware controls the power step, its default and the deliberate action to select 5 W, the tune-carrier level and timeout, and the licensee-settable receive-only guest lock (criterion b, and c as mitigation). These functions are added to the safety-critical scope of the PA enable and TX sequencer component (a delta to 03 section 4.3 for the owner's concurrence at SRR). The 6 and 30 minute key-down accumulator and the separation reminder remain convenience functions (RFX-D4).
components: PA enable and TX sequencer (power step, guest lock, tune timeout)

controls.text: Default power step 1 W at first boot and after any configuration reset; selecting 5 W requires a deliberate action distinct from tuning and volume (shared with HZ-001 K1; RFX-11).

Tune carrier at the 0.5 W step by default ending 5 s +/-0.5 s after it starts (proposed, shared with HZ-001 K2; RFX-12a; REQ-SYS-020 now bounds it to at most 5.5 s (TBR), 2 s below the 7.5 s floor of the hardware cutoff, package decision 36, OQ-SAF-005): a 0.5 W carrier at the face of a non-licensee is 21.9 percent of the general-population SAR limit and its bystander distance is 0.29 m.
controls.note: REQ-SYS-020 reads at most 5.5 s (TBR) since 2026-09-25, consistent with REQ-SYS-055; the value closes with package decision 36 (OQ-SAF-005).

controls.text: Licensee-settable receive-only guest lock that inhibits the key, the keyer and any message memory until released by a deliberate two-step action; the lock state persists across power cycles; key events in the locked state produce no PA_EN (FW-03; DECISION-7).

Operator rules card and handbook: persons other than the operator at 0.6 m or more from the antenna while keying and 1.0 m or more during a tune carrier; non-licensees key only at the 0.5 W or 1 W step with the control operator present and continuously supervising (47 CFR 97.115(b)(1)); no continuous carrier above 1 W within 20 cm of anyone; antenna gain not above 0 dBd; the licensee handing a unit to a guest sets the guest lock or the 0.5 W step first (RFX-15, DOC-02). REQ-SYS-122 checklist item 'HZ-006 K4'; REQ-SYS-123 usability runs are supporting validation only.

Convenience, not safety-critical (RFX-D4): the status display shows the selected step, a one-line separation reminder derived from the step (0.5 W 0.2 m, 1 W 0.3 m, 2 W 0.4 m, 5 W 0.6 m, tune 1.0 m) and cumulative key-down over sliding 6 and 30 minute windows at 1 s resolution (RFX-13).
The firmware stuck-key controls of HZ-004 (K3 manual-closure timeout, K4 no-gap paddle watchdog with squeeze limit) end an unintended key-down or key stream.
Permanent enclosure legend as HZ-001 K7 (licensed operators only, exposure information in the handbook).

ConOps operator model OPS-A: each licensed friend operates a unit as their own station and is responsible for its compliance (47 CFR 97.5(c), 97.103, 97.105, 97.119); unlicensed guests listen and tune freely, key only as supervised third parties, never operate a unit alone (97.7, 97.5(a), 97.109(b)); OPS-C (guest keying) is recorded as a covered misuse case, not a planned use (OPS-02, OPS-03; DECISION-6). Carried into the handbook as REQ-SYS-122 checklist item 'HZ-006 K8'; REQ-SYS-006 stores the call sign and does not implement the operator model (OQ-SAF-017).

The hardware PA-enable cutoff of HZ-004 K5 bounds any continuous carrier to 13 s, so the source-based averaging cannot be defeated by a single fault on a continuous key-down; a toggling stream is bounded in hardware only by K10 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180).

The transmission-length backstop of HZ-004 K12 (REQ-SYS-180) ends antenna-port RF, independently of firmware, after 180 s (TBR) of continuous transmit, so a single firmware fault that produces a toggling key stream cannot defeat the source-based averaging for longer than 180 s. Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (package decision 38); if the owner declines, REQ-SYS-180 is retired by the SRR decision memo and this control becomes Dropped.

residual_risk.condition: K1 to K4, K6 and K9 verified. An exceedance then needs a licensee to hand over a unit set to 5 W without the guest lock and a guest to run a carrier at the face beyond the tune timeout: an operator rule violation plus a deliberate 5 W selection. The Medium residual is accepted only with the RF exposure evaluation (RFX-18) at PDR; if the owner excludes guest keying entirely (RFX-D8: guests listen only, guest lock mandatory on hand-over) the residual falls to Critical-E, Low.

hazards.verification_note: K1 to K3, K6: HostUnit tests (defaults, confirmation gesture, tune timeout on the injected clock, guest-lock inhibit path producing no PA_EN on key events) as the closing Test (SWE-192); Emulation for event ordering only; Bench (power per step into the dummy load; guest lock demonstrated on the delivered unit). K4, K7, K8: Inspection of the handbook against the REQ-SYS-122 checklist, the rules card, the ConOps and the rendered legend by an independent reviewer. K5: HostUnit accumulator arithmetic against synthetic keying and Inspection of the display content. K9, K10: as HZ-004 K5 and K12. The general-population SAR figures close by the Analysis method (REQ-SYS-121, accepted per RSK-016) with Simulation-class evidence; the MPE distances likewise, with the antenna gain measured on the Bench at TRR.
single_point_failures: Operator discipline is the only barrier between a supervised guest and a 2 W or 5 W carrier once the guest lock is released and the step is raised; the design bounds the consequence (safe defaults, tune timeout, key-down cutoff) but cannot remove it
hazards.fault_tolerance: Single-fault tolerant against a software fault on a continuous carrier (the hardware key-down cutoff bounds the duty); a toggling key stream is bounded in hardware by K10 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180) once package decision 38 adopts it; zero-fault tolerant against an operator rule violation, which is why the rules are backed by the safe default step, the tune timeout and the guest lock.

hazards.title: Lithium-ion discharge-side fault: over-discharge, over-current, short circuit, reverse insertion, heating
hazards.description: The PA is fed directly from the protected pack (6.0 to 8.4 V, 1.3 to 2.1 A key-down pulses) through a path that bypasses the charger, so the charger's protections do not cover discharge. Discharge below 2.5 V per cell, discharge over-current, an external or internal short, a reversed or mismatched cell, mechanical damage to a cell, or heating of the cells by the PA above 60 C can lead to copper dissolution, an internal short on the next charge, venting and thermal runaway.

causes.cause: Pack discharged below 2.5 V per cell (deep discharge in use or in storage), damaging the cell for the next charge.
Short circuit on the PA rail, a failed PA device or pass element, or a conductive object dropped into the battery compartment.
Reversed cell insertion; the Keystone 1043P class holders do not prevent it; one reversed cell puts the pack near 0 V and reverse-biases the other cell.
Mixed brands, ages or capacities, a protected 69 mm cell forced into a 65 mm holder, or a cell with a damaged wrap.
PA heat conducted to the cells above 60 C during long keying in a pocket (HZ-003).
Drop or crush deforming a cell.
Leaf-spring holder contact resistance heating at 2 A key-down pulses.
Soldering or rework with cells in the holders during hand assembly: a slipped iron bridges a cell terminal or heat on a holder tab heats the cell (HZ-015 C7).

Firmware soft cut-off or discharge lock-out does not act (inaction): a cell-voltage or cell-temperature reading misscaled, stale or taken from the wrong divider, a wrong 6.4 V, 6.0 V or 60 C threshold, or a stalled battery supervision task, so the pack is discharged below 2.5 V per cell or the PA is keyed with the cells above 60 C; the protector of K1 still cuts at 2.50 V per cell independently of firmware.

Firmware enables the rails or permits transmit outside the cell window (incorrect action): rails enabled before both cells have been read, after a failed or implausible read, or with a reversed or grossly mismatched cell the K3 window check should have refused.

hazards.effects: Cell venting with flame or explosion, fire, burn injury and destruction of the unit; a shorted 18650 pair can deliver tens of amperes into a conductor and heat it to ignition. Register safety dimension 5.
hazards.rationale: Severity Catastrophic as HZ-002. Likelihood B uncontrolled: reverse insertion and mixed cells are single common operator errors by any of several users who replace the cells (SI-019, SI-023), which is the B anchor of section 3.3; a rail short is a single hardware fault; without a protector or a fuse the pack has no current limit. Re-rated from C to B after independent review. Confidence High for the protector thresholds (ABLIC datasheet), Medium for holder behaviour and cell heating by the PA.

firmware_role.statement: Firmware reads each cell through its own divider and the charger ADC, enables the rails only when both cells read 2.5 to 4.3 V, inhibits transmit below 6.4 V pack and powers down below 6.0 V (values TBR at PDR), locks out discharge above 60 C cell temperature and reports on the LCD (criteria c and e). The protector IC and the fuse act without firmware. Software causes C9 (inaction of the soft cut-off or lock-out) and C10 (rails enabled outside the window) are failures of these criterion c and e functions; they add no criterion because the firmware does not initiate the discharge-side fault, and they are bounded by the protector K1 and the fuse K2, which act without firmware.

controls.text: 2S protection IC (ABLIC S-8252 class) with a dual N-channel FET in the pack negative lead: over-discharge detect 2.50 V and release 3.00 V per cell, discharge over-current at 0.200 V across the FETs (about 5 to 10 A with a 20 to 40 mohm pair), load short at 0.500 V, internal delay timers, quiescent current below 10 uA (D-PWR-03). The protector class, its thresholds and the dual N-FET are Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (D-PWR-03, package decision 72).

tbr.item: Discharge over-current trip level 5 to 10 A
tbr.plan: Fixed by the dual N-FET selection (RDS(on), SOA at 10 A pulses) in A-PWR-03 at PDR.

controls.text: PCB fuse or PTC in the pack lead rated for the 2.1 A key-down pulses and opening on a sustained short (rating in A-PWR-03).

Reverse and mismatch protection: the protector FETs stay off unless both cells are within window (blocks the reversed-cell and grossly mismatched cases); 300 ohm in series with the MID sense; per-cell dividers referenced to pack negative; firmware enables the rails only after both cells read 2.5 to 4.3 V and their difference is below 300 mV (TBR as HZ-002 K5).

Soft cut-off per cell: transmit inhibited while either cell reads below 3.20 V +/-0.05 V (REQ-SYS-097) and power-down when either cell reads below 3.00 V +/-0.05 V (REQ-SYS-098), TBR (6.4 V and 6.0 V for a balanced pack); discharge lock-out at 60 C cell temperature read through the charger TS input; battery gauge and low-battery warning on the LCD (SWE-134 h, j).

tbr.item: 6.4 V transmit inhibit and 6.0 V power-down thresholds
tbr.plan: Set at PDR from the digitised discharge curve of the chosen cell (A-PWR-07) and the PA output floor at 6.0 V.

controls.text: Cells retained in holders with polarity marked in the compartment and on the enclosure, separated from the PA thermal zone by distance or a barrier, an enclosure vent path with no sealed cavity, no sharp edges near the cells, and a closed compartment that admits no conductive object (RSK-007 S4). REQ-SYS-086 (survive a reversed cell) does not implement the compartment or the marking; the requirement is requested in OQ-SAF-010.
Reverse-polarity P-FET on the rail feed; mechanical power switch on the buck enable and the PA rail (charger and protector always live at about 25 uA) (D-PWR-08).

Handbook: approved cell list (one brand and age, matched capacity), insertion procedure with the polarity marks, do not use damaged or mismatched cells, storage at partial charge with the radio switched off.

residual_risk.condition: Protector, fuse and firmware checks verified (REQ-SYS-084, REQ-SYS-086, REQ-SYS-087, REQ-SYS-096 to REQ-SYS-099 by Test; REQ-SYS-085 by the Analysis method accepted per RSK-007 unless OQ-SAF-018 converts it to a component-level Test); residual Medium (Catastrophic-E) requires the owner's acceptance at SAR under the RSK-007 acceptance record. The compartment control K5 is requirement pending and does not count (section 3.5); a conductive object in the compartment is still bounded by two independent devices (protector and fuse). Per-cell under-voltage detection shares the MID sense single point of HZ-002, whose next-charge consequence HZ-002 carries.

hazards.verification_note: K1: REQ-SYS-084 over-discharge: Bench with a bench supply substituting for each cell as the closing Test (trip and release). K1, K2: REQ-SYS-085 over-current and short closes today by the Analysis method accepted per RSK-007, with Simulation-class evidence (protector trip voltage over FET resistance and temperature; fuse or PTC rating against the 2.1 A key-down pulses); a component-level Test is requested (0.200 V injected at the protector sense pin from a bench supply; short-circuit test at reduced voltage from a current-limited source; OQ-SAF-018), and until it is adopted the Bench over-current and short checks are supporting evidence, not closing. K3, K4: HostUnit fault injection (reversed cell reading, mismatch, low pack, hot cell) as the closing Test (SWE-192) and Bench with a reversed dummy cell at reduced voltage. K5, K6: Inspection of the enclosure model, the layout and the delivered unit; Bench thermal measurement of cell temperature after a 5 minute key-down. K7: Inspection. C9, C10: covered by the K3 and K4 HostUnit fault-injection cases (misscaled, stale and failed cell reads; out-of-window cells at rail enable) as the closing Test, with the K1 protector trip on the Bench as the firmware-independent bound.
single_point_failures: Protector FET pair (a shorted FET removes the over-current and over-discharge cut): the fuse backs over-current and short; nothing in hardware backs over-discharge except the firmware soft cut-off, which is a dissimilar software layer
Holder leaf-spring contact (high resistance heats at 2 A; an open contact stops the radio safely)

Shared MID sense net (HZ-002 K9): one open or high-resistance sense connection blinds per-cell under-voltage detection in the protector and the firmware alike, so one cell can be driven below 2.5 V while the pack reads above 6.0 V; the damage shows at the next charge, whose consequence HZ-002 carries; removed only by the Kelvin sense constraint (OQ-SAF-009)
hazards.fault_tolerance: Single-fault tolerant for short and over-current (protector plus fuse, independent devices); single-fault tolerant for over-discharge (protector plus firmware soft cut-off, dissimilar); reverse insertion is blocked by the protector window and detected by firmware before any rail is enabled.
