hazards.title: Harmonic and spurious emissions into safety-of-life and other radio services
hazards.description: Harmonics of the 144 to 148 MHz carrier fall on: 2f 288 to 296 MHz (US Federal fixed and mobile, military only, footnotes G27 G100); 3f 432 to 444 MHz (Federal radiolocation primary, 70 cm amateur secondary including the 432.300 to 432.400 MHz beacon segment and amateur-satellite 435 to 438 MHz); 4f 576 to 592 MHz (UHF TV channels 31 to 33); 5f 720 to 740 MHz (commercial 700 MHz mobile); 7f 1008 to 1036 MHz (aeronautical radionavigation: DME/TACAN and the 1030 MHz SSR/IFF interrogation frequency, footnote US78). The legal spurious limit at 5 W is 53 dB below the carrier (47 CFR 97.307(e): not above 25 uW and at least 40 dB down for transmitters of 25 W or less); the raw 2fo of the baseline PA line-up is only 37 to 40 dB down. Keying sidebands and frequency-reference error can also cross the 144.000 and 148.000 MHz band edges (97.307(b)), and the Pico 2 12 MHz crystal (12th harmonic) and 48 MHz USB clock (3rd harmonic) land on 144.000 MHz as receiver birdies. A gross frequency-control error places the fundamental itself outside the band: the harmonic low-pass filter (at most 0.5 dB loss at 148 MHz, 40 dB at 288 MHz) has its cutoff between 148 and 288 MHz and passes much of 150 to 174 MHz, which carries VHF public-safety and maritime services including the 156.8 MHz distress, safety and calling channel (allocation not yet in the project corpus, OQ-SAF-024), so a single frequency-control software fault can put 5 W there.

causes.cause: PA raw harmonics (measured RD07MUS2B line-up 2fo -37 to -40 dBc, 3fo -62 to -65 dBc at 5 W; RA07M1317M module maxima -25 and -30 dBc) without adequate low-pass filtering.
Filter component failure, inductor self-resonance, or layout leakage around the filter.
A PIN-diode T/R switch placed after the filter regenerating harmonics (not applicable to the relay baseline, SI-036).

Output above 5 W at full charge (8.5 to 10 W without ALC) raising absolute harmonic levels by 3 dB; a gate-bias keying ramp degrading 2fo toward -17 dBc at low power (raw absolute level up to +8.5 dBm).
Hard keying (no envelope shaping) producing keyclicks out to 1.1 kHz, or a plain-crystal reference (+/-20 to 30 ppm) placing the 26 dB bandwidth across a band edge.
PA instability (parasitic oscillation) producing non-harmonic spurious emissions (RSK-001).

Frequency-control software fault (a wrong divider or register computation, a corrupted frequency word, a calibration value out of range) placing the carrier outside 144 to 148 MHz, for example on 150 to 174 MHz; REQ-SYS-009 checks the set frequency inside the same component and cannot see a wrong synthesized output.
Synthesizer hardware fault: the PLL unlocked, locked to a wrong value or to a reference harmonic, so the output differs grossly from the commanded frequency.

hazards.effects: Interference to an aeronautical radionavigation service, which 47 CFR 97.3(a)(23) treats as harmful interference per se (the 1030 MHz SSR/IFF interrogation frequency is a safety-of-life system); interference to Federal radiolocation and to 70 cm weak-signal and beacon operation by the project's own community; violation of 97.307(e) and 97.307(b). The radiated 7th-harmonic level from a handheld at or below -16 dBm is far below aeronautical receiver thresholds at any realistic separation (analysis not done, Low confidence), so the aircraft case is a regulatory and good-practice concern rather than a demonstrated danger; the regulatory rule of 06 section 7 scores any 97.307 exceedance at least 4. A 5 W carrier on a VHF public-safety or maritime channel (156.8 MHz distress and calling) from a frequency-control fault is harmful interference to a safety service (47 CFR 97.3(a)(23)), Critical on the section 3.2 scale, and needs no harmonic path at all.
hazards.rationale: Severity Critical because the worst credible effect is harmful interference to a safety service (radionavigation), this analysis's Critical definition, and because a 97.307 exceedance is at least level 4 under the register's regulatory rule. Likelihood C uncontrolled: without the low-pass filter every 5 W transmission exceeds the 53 dBc requirement at 2f (raw -37 to -40 dBc); an actual interference event additionally needs a victim receiver nearby, which is occasional at most. Confidence Medium: harmonic data are from one vendor lot in one evaluation circuit (2011) and the 2.106 rows rest on the 2022 FCC table plus Federal Register amendatory text. The frequency-control cause C7 is also Critical-C: one software fault is enough and the only check, REQ-SYS-009, lives in the same component; a victim receiver within range is occasional.

firmware_role.statement: Frequency control causes or contributes to the out-of-band fundamental of C7 (criterion a): one fault in the frequency-word path can put 5 W on 150 to 174 MHz, which the harmonic filter passes. The proposed independent frequency verification K7 mitigates it (criterion c) and detects, reports and inhibits (criterion e). This supersedes the PHA 0.1.0 determination that frequency control is mission-critical only, whose basis (a firmware fault moves the harmonic level by at most 3 dB) covered harmonics only; the change is a proposed delta to 03 section 4.3 for the owner's concurrence at SRR (hazard-analysis.md section 6.3 item 6). The ALC set-point and the keying envelope remain mission-critical: an ALC or envelope fault raises harmonics by at most 3 dB or widens the keying sidebands, both absorbed by the 7 dB filter margin and the 1 kHz band-edge guard.
components: Frequency control (SW-SYNTH: frequency-word computation, calibration application, band-edge limit, register write with read-back; proposed safety-critical for C7)
Frequency verification unit (SW-SAFE, independent of SW-SYNTH; proposed, REQ-SYS-182, package decision 40)
PA enable and TX sequencer (frequency-verified PA_EN prerequisite)

controls.text: Transmit low-pass filter at the antenna port after the T/R node, measured at its own terminals: at least 40 dB at 288 to 296 MHz and 35 dB at 432 to 444 MHz with insertion loss not above 0.5 dB at 148 MHz; the assembled transmitter meets a 60 dBc design target for every spurious emission at every instant of the keying envelope (7 dB margin over the 53 dBc legal minimum at 5 W).

PA device with measured VHF harmonic data (the device TS-001 selects at PDR from BOM-linkable stocked parts per SI-028 and ADR-012; TS-001 recommends PD54008L-E; the Mitsubishi RD07MUS2B, whose measured line-up harmonics set the present filter goals, is consignment-only and excluded by ADR-012 unless the owner waives it) so the filter goal covers the raw levels; the sequenced RF relay of the semi break-in baseline (TE Axicom HF3 class, SI-036) generates no harmonics; any PIN switch, if ever adopted, sits before the filter (TR-05).

ALC (gate-bias loop with a forward-power detector) holds the selected step to +/-0.5 dB from 6.4 to 8.4 V; firmware over-voltage lockout above about 8.6 V; every element after the PA rated for the full-charge, full-drive output (10 W class) unless the ALC is shown by analysis to limit power under all single faults; detector reading plausibility-checked (SWE-134 g). REQ-SYS-012 covers the ALC; no requirement states the over-voltage lockout (OQ-SAF-015).

Raised-cosine keying envelope, 5 ms 10-to-90 percent (3 to 8 ms configurable, not speed-adaptive, no mid-ramp reversal, minimum radiated element one full ramp) giving a measured 26 dB bandwidth not above 350 Hz at 50 WPM with continuous dits; carrier limited to 144.001 to 147.999 MHz with a TCXO reference of +/-2.5 ppm or better independent of the Pico 2 crystal; necessary bandwidth documented as 208HA1A.

Spurious verification before any antenna-connected transmission: NanoVNA S21 of the assembled filter; tinySA Ultra (SI-034) with a calibrated attenuator at 5 W into the dummy load reporting 2f, 3f and 7f individually with the victim service named against the 60 dB target, and the band edges with max-hold over continuous dits; RF only into the dummy load until the Part 97 cases pass; PA small-signal stability analysis (Rollett K and mu, 1 MHz to 1 GHz) at CDR (RSK-001 S2, S3; RSK-011).

Clock plan avoiding harmonics on 144.000 MHz where possible: USB PLL off when not enumerated, SPI and PWM clock choices per the clock-harmonic table, the 5 V buck synchronised to a firmware-set frequency; expected birdies predicted and logged before the TRR birdie survey.

Independent frequency verification before PA_EN: a sample of the transmit synthesizer output, divided by a hardware prescaler, is counted by a PIO or timer unit that is separate from the synthesizer driver and uses the RP2350 crystal timebase rather than the synthesizer reference; PA_EN is permitted only when the counted frequency agrees with the set frequency within 10 kHz (TBR) and the set frequency, held with its complement, lies inside 144.001 to 147.999 MHz; a disagreement enters Fault-safe with the cause shown. It catches the gross errors of C7 and C8 that REQ-SYS-009 cannot; the 1 kHz guard stays with REQ-SYS-008, REQ-SYS-009 and the TCXO. A hardware band-selective element on the TX path was rejected: attenuating 156.8 MHz while passing 148 MHz with at most 0.5 dB loss needs a high-order filter with loss the 5 W budget cannot carry. Implemented by REQ-SYS-182 (Independent frequency verification before and during transmit, Draft, 10 kHz TBR; OQ-SAF-013), the measurement and the transmit permit, and REQ-SYS-154, the Fault-safe response to a disagreement found during transmission. Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (package decision 40, taken with decision 9); if the owner declines, REQ-SYS-182 is retired by the SRR decision memo and this control becomes Dropped.

tbr.plan: Set at PDR from the counter resolution and the 30 ppm crystal timebase tolerance (about 4.4 kHz at 146 MHz) with margin; the prescaler and counter design is a PDR item.

residual_risk.condition: Harmonic branch: filter response and transmitter spectrum verified by Bench (tinySA Ultra) on every unit before on-air use, so a harmonic exceedance needs a filter component failure after acceptance and a nearby victim receiver (E). Frequency-control branch: with the independent frequency verification K7 (REQ-SYS-182 with the REQ-SYS-154 response, Proposed, package decision 40 taken with decision 9) verified, a gross frequency-word fault in SW-SYNTH is caught before PA_EN and during transmission by a count that shares neither that component nor the synthesizer reference, so an out-of-band carrier needs the frequency-control fault plus a failure of the verification (E): Critical-E, Low. If the owner declines package decision 40, REQ-SYS-182 is retired, K7 becomes Dropped (REQ-SYS-154 remains, its off-frequency detection no longer independent of SW-SYNTH) and the residual is Critical-D, Medium: a single frequency-word fault that escapes REQ-SYS-008 and REQ-SYS-009 in SW-SYNTH and the HZ-014 configuration guard places 5 W out of band, and an interference event also needs a victim within range (one fault plus an uncommon condition). Section 3.4 accepts that Medium only with the listed controls allocated and verified and the owner's acceptance at SAR, and the SRR decision memo then records single point failure row 4 of hazard-analysis.md section 8.2 as an accepted single point; concurrence with decision 9 alone does not change the level (section 6.3 item 6).

hazards.verification_note: K1: Simulation (S-parameter simulation with vendor inductor models including self-resonance, tolerance corners; checker on the LTspice output) then Bench (NanoVNA S21 of the filter, including its response from 148 to 174 MHz; tinySA Ultra with attenuator for the transmitter at 5 W into the dummy load, 2f, 3f and 7f reported individually). K2, K3: Inspection (device data, sourcing) and Bench (power per step across 6.0 to 8.4 V, harmonic levels during the keying ramp with max-hold). K4: Simulation (FFT of the captured envelope, reference budget) and Bench (tinySA at the band edges, off-air reference); REQ-SYS-010 closes by the Analysis method accepted per RSK-002 (no frequency counter). K5: Inspection of the TRR procedure and reports. K6: Simulation (harmonic table) and Bench birdie survey. K7 (REQ-SYS-182, REQ-SYS-154): Inspection of the schematic and the software design for the independence of the counter, its timebase and its component from SW-SYNTH; HostUnit with injected counter readings (in band, wrong divider, corrupted word, out-of-range calibration, counter fault) as the closing Test (SWE-192); Bench, a fault-injection build commanding a frequency word for 156.8 MHz with the PA disconnected, PA_EN confirmed low and the fault shown. Regulatory requirements are verified on the delivered unit, never by Analysis alone (charter section 9; 06 section 14.1 class 1g), except the RSK-002 frequency-accuracy acceptance.
single_point_failures: Low-pass filter (a single open or shorted element removes the attenuation at 2f or 3f): detected only by measurement; accepted for a hand-built series of at most 5 units with a Bench measurement of every unit at ATP and a filter test point for the NanoVNA (RSK-011 S3)

ALC forward-power detector (a failed detector reading low drives full output, 10 W at full charge): bounded by device saturation and the filter margin; firmware plausibility check on the detector reading (SWE-134 g)

Frequency-word path in SW-SYNTH (a single software fault can place 5 W on 150 to 174 MHz, which the harmonic filter passes; REQ-SYS-009 checks the set frequency in the same component): removed by the independent frequency verification K7 (REQ-SYS-182) if the owner adopts package decision 40; an accepted single point if declined (OQ-SAF-013)
hazards.fault_tolerance: Zero-fault tolerant in hardware for the filter (a single filter, measured per unit); single-fault tolerant for over-power (ALC plus device saturation plus 7 dB filter margin); single-fault tolerant for band-edge crossing by keying sidebands or reference drift (1 kHz guard plus TCXO plus firmware frequency limits); single-fault tolerant for a gross frequency-control fault with K7 (REQ-SYS-182), and zero-fault tolerant for it if package decision 40 declines K7, because the only other check (REQ-SYS-009) is in the same component.

hazards.title: Antenna connector mechanical failure and PCB damage
hazards.description: The whip (0.40 m NA-771 class, 0.48 m Signal Stick, or a 1.02 m half-wave telescopic) is screwed to an SMA jack on the end of a pocket radio. A side load of 5 to 10 N at the tip of a 0.40 m whip (a finger push, a pocket snag, a fall onto the antenna) produces 2.0 to 4.0 N.m at the connector, which reaches the yield moment of a brass SMA neck (2.4 to 3.6 N.m); a PCB-only mounted jack transfers that moment into solder joints and copper, which fail first. Brass SMA jacks are rated for 100 matings and stainless MIL-PRF-39012 class jacks for 500; the owner and friends swap antennas often.

causes.cause: Jack mounted on the PCB only, carrying the antenna moment into solder joints and copper.
Fall onto the antenna, pocket snag, sitting on the radio, leverage from a 1 m telescopic whip.
Brass jack worn out by matings, or over-torque with a wrench (limit 0.45 to 0.56 N.m for brass).
Tolerance stack of a PCB-mount bulkhead jack nutted through the lid pre-loads the solder joints or leaves the nut unable to seat.
Anodize under the jack flange insulating the shell from the chassis (loss of counterpoise and RF ground, arcing at the joint).

hazards.effects: Broken connector neck or torn PCB pads: loss of the radio (hidden-pad rework is not available to the owner, SI-009, SI-031); the PA then transmits into an open or intermittent load (HZ-003 C6); a broken stub with a sharp edge (first aid); an intermittent RF ground raising RF on the cables and the chassis (HZ-010, HZ-012). Register safety dimension 3.
hazards.rationale: Severity Marginal: destruction of the unit without fire and at most a first-aid cut from a broken stub. Likelihood B uncontrolled: a pocket radio's antenna is loaded daily; repair forums describe SMA failure as common wear and tear and document boards with the SMA broken off. Confidence Medium for the bending analysis (material properties assumed), High for the connector ratings (Amphenol RF Europe and AEP catalogs).

firmware_role.statement: None; a mechanical hazard with no firmware role.

controls.text: SMA jack (female body, 1/4-36 UNS-2A thread, stainless steel, 500 mating cycle class) retained to the machined enclosure by its bulkhead nut through a boss at least 2.5 mm thick, hole 6.55 mm +0.05/-0.00, an anti-rotation flat and clearance for the 7.9 mm hex nut; the PCB connection carries no antenna moment (an RG-316 pigtail to a board connector, or a PCB-mount bulkhead jack with a documented tolerance stack of about 0.3 mm between PCB outline, standoff height and lid hole).

The antenna port withstands a static bending moment of 4.0 N.m in any direction (10 N at 0.40 m) and 500 mating cycles at 0.45 to 0.56 N.m coupling torque without loss of RF continuity, PCB damage or rotation of the jack (ANT-02; the research candidate's 1000 cycles exceeds any rated SMA and is corrected here to the stainless rating).

The transmitter delivers rated power at SWR up to 2:1 and survives 60 s of continuous key-down into any load up to 10:1 at any phase and into open and short circuits without damage (ANT-04); optional forward and reverse power detector with fold-back above SWR 3:1 (antenna DECISION-5).

Chassis ground and connector contact areas masked from anodize and shown on the drawing; a counterpoise attachment (ring terminal under the SMA nut or an M3 hole in the boss) within 20 mm of the port with DC resistance to the connector shell at or below 10 mohm (ANT-03).

Reference pocket antenna is a flexible Nitinol whip (Signal Stick SMA-M) plus a 48 cm counterpoise; handbook: finger-tight only, never a wrench; remove the antenna for pocket carry; use a 1 m telescopic only with the radio on a surface (ANT-05).

Printed (H2C) fit-check of the boss, jack and nut with the real PCB before the CNC order; static load test of 10 N at 0.40 m on the printed part and on the first machined enclosure; tolerance analysis in the PDR package (ANT-R6).

residual_risk.condition: Boss load path verified by the static load test on the machined enclosure and the PA survival into open and short verified on the bench.

hazards.verification_note: K1, K2: Simulation (hand calculation or FEA of the boss and jack neck; tolerance analysis), Bench (static 10 N at 0.40 m on the printed fit-check part and on the first machined enclosure) and Inspection (nut torque, thread engagement, anti-rotation flat); REQ-SYS-106 (mating life) closes by the Analysis method from the datasheet cycle rating plus Inspection, with NanoVNA return loss at receipt and at SAR as supporting Bench evidence. K3: Simulation (SPICE at load extremes with the filter) and Bench (NanoVNA-characterised mismatch fixtures, 60 s key-down, temperature check). K4: Inspection and Bench (resistance at or below 10 mohm by a current-injection measurement with the bench supply and the multimeter). K5: Inspection. K6: Inspection of the fit-check report.
single_point_failures: The single antenna jack: designed so that the enclosure boss, not the jack or the PCB, is the load path; a broken jack still fails to an open load that the PA survives (K3)
hazards.fault_tolerance: Fail-safe by design: the load path is the enclosure; a connector failure leaves the PA into an open load that the device tolerates for at least 60 s, so the residual is loss of function, not injury.
decisions_pending: Antenna DECISION-1: SMA jack with the ANT-02 load path (recommended) versus BNC bulkhead
Antenna DECISION-2: Signal Stick SMA-M plus 48 cm tail as the pocket reference (recommended)
Antenna DECISION-5: SWR fold-back detector versus PA ruggedness alone (PDR)

hazards.title: ESD and RF pickup on the key, paddle and headphone inputs
hazards.description: The key/paddle jack and the headphone jack are touched and cabled by hand, and the paddle and headphone leads (1.0 to 1.5 m, unshielded) hang within centimetres of a 5 W antenna (near-field estimate of the order of 100 V/m at 0.1 m). A contact discharge of 8 kV (IEC 61000-4-2 level 4) or RF pickup can damage the RP2350 pads (HBM 2 kV, absolute maximum -0.5 to +5.5 V), cause a false key closure (HZ-004) or a false opening, produce an audio thump (HZ-005) or reset the controller during transmission.

causes.cause: Electrostatic discharge from the operator's body into a jack contact or an inserted plug in dry conditions.
RF current on the paddle or headphone cable coupled into the key input or the audio return during 5 W keying.
An external keyer with a positive keying line (+12 V) or an audio source connected to the key jack (abuse bound -5 V to +12 V continuous, TBR).

RP2350 erratum E9 leakage (A2 stepping) if an input sits in the undefined region, lowering the open-contact voltage (silicon behaviour; the reset-default pull-down part of the former C4 is now the Software cause C6).
Headphone output shorted by a TS plug or by a key cross-plugged into the PHONES jack.

Firmware key-input pad configuration wrong (incorrect action): the reset-default pull-down left enabled, the Schmitt trigger off or the pad left input-disabled by the keyer's pico2 GPIO initialisation, lowering the open-contact voltage into the undefined region or reading an open contact as closed (split from the former C4).

Firmware debounce or stuck-input detection misclassifies an input (incorrect action or inaction): a wrong debounce constant or sample period passes RF-pickup or ESD pulses as closures, or a persistent closure from a damaged clamp is not flagged to the HZ-004 interlock and timeouts.

hazards.effects: Latent or immediate damage to an RP2350 pad or the audio amplifier (loss of the radio); false keying events (unintended transmission, HZ-004) or false openings (broken elements); audio thumps and level changes with cable position (HZ-005 startle); a controller reset during transmission. Register safety dimension 3 (unit loss) with the injury consequences carried by HZ-004 and HZ-005.
hazards.rationale: Severity Marginal: damage to the unit and consequences routed through HZ-004 and HZ-005; no direct injury. Likelihood B uncontrolled: 8 kV discharges from a hand on a jack in winter and RF on a 1 m paddle cable at 5 W are both routine in handheld use. Confidence High for the RP2350 and clamp figures (datasheets quoted), Medium for the RF attenuation (layout and parasitics).

firmware_role.statement: Firmware debounces both key inputs (2 ms make, 5 ms open, TBR closing by PDR with REQ-SYS-048), treats a persistent closure by the HZ-004 interlock and timeouts, and range-checks the jack-detect inputs (criterion c, SWE-134 g); the ESD and RF protection itself is hardware. The keyer component is already safety-critical through HZ-004. Software causes C6 (pad configuration) and C7 (debounce or stuck-input misclassification) are failures of this criterion c function; the keyer component is already safety-critical with criteria a, b and c through HZ-004, so the component list and its criteria are unchanged.
components: Keyer and keying output (debounce, stuck-input detection)

controls.text: Per key line from the jack: optional 100 pF C0G shunt at the connector, TI TPD2E2U06 class unidirectional clamp (IEC 61000-4-2 level 4, 8 kV contact and 15 kV air) covering tip and ring, 1.0 kohm series resistor, 10 kohm pull-up to 3V3, 4.7 nF at the pad node, BAT54S dual Schottky secondary clamp to 3V3 and ground; survives -5 V to +12 V continuous on either contact (CTL-KEY-03, CTL-KEY-04).

tbr.item: Abuse bound -5 V to +12 V continuous
tbr.owner: Robin confirms the external-keyer use case (D-KN7)
tbr.plan: If a +24 V keying line must be supported the series resistor moves to a 1206 package; decided at PDR with ICD-CTL-KEY.

controls.text: Pad configured input-enabled with the Schmitt trigger on, internal pull-up and pull-down off, read active-low; closed-contact pad voltage below 0.6 V with a 500 ohm contact allowance including 120 uA E9 leakage; the 1 kohm and 4.7 nF network attenuates 144 MHz cable pickup by about 70 dB before the 0.2 V hysteresis (an Inspection item on the pad configuration bits).

Debounce 2 ms make and 5 ms open at a 1 kHz sample rate (fixed counts of 2 and 5 consecutive samples per REQ-SW-KEYER-020 and 021, not operator-configurable, TBR until the owner's key and paddle bounce is captured, closing by PDR with REQ-SYS-048); a persistent closure is handled by the HZ-004 interlock and timeouts. A key input that reads closed with no plug present withholds key-down (REQ-SW-KEYER-036).

Common-mode suppression (ferrite or choke plus bypass, impedance at or above 500 ohm at 146 MHz) on the key and headphone lines, so that keying 5 W into any reference antenna produces no false keyer input and no audible change with 1.0 to 1.5 m unshielded leads (ANT-06).
Headphone outputs survive an indefinite short to sleeve (TS plug, cross-plugged key) and ESD as K1; amplifier with short-circuit protection; jack detection debounced 50 ms (CTL-AUD-03).

Bench RF-immunity case: key the transmitter into the dummy load from memory while 1.5 m unshielded leads hang on the key and headphone jacks (REQ-SYS-051) and confirm zero false state changes in a 5 minute logic capture (CTL-KEY-05); the ESD rating is shown by Analysis of the clamp datasheets because no ESD generator is on the bench.

residual_risk.condition: Input network inspected against ICD-CTL-KEY and the bench RF-immunity case passed on the delivered unit.

hazards.verification_note: K1, K2: Simulation (network arithmetic, clamp current at 8 kV and at the abuse bound) and Inspection (schematic, pad configuration bits against the RP2350 datasheet, ICD-CTL-KEY); Bench multimeter on the pad node with the contact closed and open; REQ-SYS-050 (ESD) closes by the Analysis method because no ESD generator is on the bench. K3: HostUnit debounce vectors as the closing Test (SWE-192) and Bench capture of the owner's key and paddle bounce (closes the debounce TBR by PDR). K4, K6: Bench RF-immunity case. K5: Simulation (amplifier short-circuit data, audio report ACTION A2) and Bench. C6: Inspection of the pad configuration bits in the pico2 GPIO initialisation against the RP2350 datasheet (driver-to-datasheet traceability) and the Bench open-contact pad voltage of K2. C7: the K3 HostUnit debounce vectors (REQ-SW-KEYER-019 to REQ-SW-KEYER-021) with injected RF-pickup pulses and a persistent closure.
single_point_failures: TVS clamp (an open clamp leaves the 1 kohm series resistor and the BAT54S as the only protection: still bounded for the abuse case, degraded for 8 kV ESD): accepted with Inspection
hazards.fault_tolerance: Single-fault tolerant for ESD (two clamp stages plus series resistance); RF pickup is controlled by attenuation margin (about 70 dB) plus debounce plus the HZ-004 interlock and verified by the bench immunity case.

hazards.title: Charging while transmitting
hazards.description: USB charging through the Pico 2 micro-USB (input budget 2.5 W at 500 mA; the module's VBUS path is not rated above 500 mA) while the PA draws 1.3 to 2.1 A key-down pulses from the pack. The baseline prevents the state: the transmitter is inhibited by hardware whenever VBUS is present (ConOps Charging mode and the forbidden transition 'Transmit-keyed while USB power is present'; REQ-SYS-092), and charging is paused while the radio is switched on (REQ-SYS-093). The hazard is the state in which the inhibit fails and the charger runs while the PA is keyed: the charger's 1.5 MHz boost ripple on the pack appears on the PA drain, the charger's input and DPM loops respond to the key-down steps, the input budget cannot carry transmit power, and charge termination is disturbed by the load.

causes.cause: Keying while the USB cable is connected to a laptop or a wall adapter, or plugging USB in during an over.
Firmware fails to disarm transmit on the VBUS sense GPIO, or leaves charging enabled while the radio is switched on.
Hardware transmit inhibit absent or failed: its VBUS sense divider open (reads no VBUS) or the inhibit element failed in the permit state.
USB source current above 500 mA through the Pico 2 connector, D1 diode and VBUS copper, an unqualified path (R-PWR-01).

hazards.effects: AM sidebands at +/-1.5 MHz from the boost ripple that count as spurious emissions (47 CFR 97.307(e)); charger fault loops and false termination (over- or under-charge, feeding HZ-002 C7); heating of the micro-USB connector, D1 and VBUS trace above their unqualified current (a low-energy but real burn and ignition source in a pocket radio); a laptop port pushed past its 500 mA budget. Register safety dimension 3.
hazards.rationale: Severity Marginal: connector or trace heating and a spurious-emission violation without a safety-service victim; the overcharge path is carried by HZ-002. Likelihood B uncontrolled: operators will transmit with the charger connected unless prevented. Confidence Low on the Pico 2 VBUS path rating (unpublished), High on the charger behaviour (datasheet).

firmware_role.statement: Firmware reads VBUS on GPIO24 and disarms transmit while USB power is present (a PA_EN prerequisite and the ConOps forbidden transition), pauses charging while the radio is switched on, and reports the charge state and the inhibit (criteria c and e). The hardware transmit inhibit on its own VBUS sense acts without firmware.

controls.text: Hardware transmit inhibit with USB power: a VBUS sense divider of its own (not the Pico 2 GPIO24 divider) forces the PA-path enable low whenever VBUS is present, independently of firmware, preferably at the same PA-path gate as HZ-004 K5 (PDR); a key closure with USB applied produces no RF.

Charging paused while the power switch is on and USB power is present (receive allowed while charging, D-PWR-07 recommended default), so termination is not masked and the charger's boost ripple is absent whenever the radio is operating; the LCD shows the charge state. A hardware implementation (the power switch driving the charger CD pin) is a PDR option.

The radio never transmits from USB power alone: the PA rail comes only from the protected pack; with no cells inserted only the Pico 2 is powered from VBUS, so firmware loading with the cells removed cannot energise the transmitter (F22). REQ-SYS-149 (No transmitter supply from USB alone: transmitter supply below 0.5 V TBR while powered from USB with the cells removed) states the topology as a measurable limit (OQ-SAF-011 closed); owner decision D-PWR-07 pending at SRR (package decision 75).

Input current limit 500 mA by default (PSEL strap and register default), never above 1.5 A, and above 500 mA only after DCP or CDP identification or an explicit charging-port setting; the Pico 2 VBUS path current bounded by a measured or vendor-confirmed rating (A-PWR-01) and by the 500 mA design limit until then (PWR-USB-01, PWR-USB-02).

Handbook: charging state on the LCD; transmit is inhibited whenever USB power is present; charge with the radio off or receiving; use a supply rated for 500 mA or more (REQ-SYS-122 checklist item 'HZ-011 K5').

Firmware transmit inhibit on the VBUS sense GPIO (GPIO24), the dissimilar layer of K1 on a separate sense path: transmit is disarmed and VBUS absent is a PA_EN prerequisite (SWE-134 h), the ConOps forbidden transition 'Transmit-keyed while USB power is present' (REQ-SYS-002); VBUS applied during an over ends it through the normal envelope fall within one sample. REQ-SYS-002 lists HZ-011 in its hazard_ids (OQ-SAF-011 closed).

residual_risk.condition: K1 hardware inhibit and K6 firmware inhibit verified on the bench with USB applied and TX_KEY forced, and K2 verified: charging while transmitting then needs the hardware inhibit on its own VBUS sense and the firmware inhibit on GPIO24 to fail together, and the charge pause as well for the ripple path. The Pico 2 VBUS path rating measured (A-PWR-01) or the 500 mA limit kept. K3 (REQ-SYS-149) adds the supply topology: with the cells removed the transmitter has no supply, whatever the inhibits do.

hazards.verification_note: K1: Simulation of the inhibit path; Bench as the closing Test: a fault-injection build asserting TX_KEY and PA_EN with USB applied, RF into the dummy load read on the tinySA Ultra and the PA-path enable logged (REQ-SYS-092), repeated with the GPIO24 sense disconnected so that only the hardware path acts. K2: HostUnit of the charge-control state as the closing Test (SWE-192); Bench, charge current read with the switch off and on. K3: Inspection of the schematic and Bench at stage 4 of the power-on sequence (USB only, no cells: PA rail absent). K4: Inspection of the strap and registers; Bench with a current-limited supply at 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 A including the Pico 2 VBUS path voltage drop and temperature. K5: Inspection. K6: HostUnit (VBUS present makes the PA_EN prerequisite false; the forbidden transition of REQ-SYS-002) as the closing Test and Bench with the hardware inhibit disabled in a test build.

Inhibit element failed in the permit state: K1 lost; backed by K6 and K2
Pico 2 VBUS path (unrated by the vendor): bounded by the 500 mA design limit until measured
hazards.fault_tolerance: Single-fault tolerant: the hardware inhibit (own VBUS sense) and the firmware inhibit (GPIO24 sense) are dissimilar and on separate sense paths; the charge pause while switched on removes the charger ripple even if both inhibits fail; the input current limit bounds the connector current regardless of any of them.

hazards.title: RF burn from contact with the antenna element or connector while transmitting
hazards.description: At 5 W the antenna port carries 15.8 V rms (22.4 V peak) into 50 ohm and up to 44.7 V peak into an open or short circuit; the tip of an end-fed half-wave whip is a voltage maximum where the RF voltage is of the order of 100 V rms at 5 W (end impedance of a few kohm; a derived order-of-magnitude figure, Low confidence). Touching the whip tip, an exposed connector centre contact, the whip base or the end of the counterpoise wire while keyed can cause a localized RF burn.

causes.cause: Touching or adjusting the whip or the counterpoise while keying or during a tune carrier.
Exposed metal at the whip base or an uncovered counterpoise wire end.
Antenna removed while keyed (open port, doubled voltage) and a finger on the centre contact.
A stuck carrier (HZ-004) keeping the voltage present without the operator's intent.

hazards.effects: Localized RF burn (first aid, a small blister) at the contact point and a startle reaction; no electric-shock hazard at these voltages and at 144 MHz (RF above 100 kHz does not stimulate nerves). Register safety dimension 3.
hazards.rationale: Severity Marginal: a first-aid burn at most; 22 to 45 V peak at the port is well inside the connector's 500 V rating and causes no shock. Likelihood C uncontrolled: adjusting a telescopic whip during a tune carrier is an occasional operator action, and the burn threshold at 5 W is reached only near the high-impedance end of a half-wave whip. Confidence Medium (the port voltages are arithmetic; the tip voltage is an estimate).

firmware_role.statement: Firmware controls the tune-carrier level and timeout and the power step (criterion b) and the timeouts that bound a stuck carrier (criterion c), the same functions as HZ-001.
components: PA enable and TX sequencer (tune timeout, power step)

controls.text: Tune carrier at the 0.5 W step by default ending 5 s +/-0.5 s after it starts (proposed; REQ-SYS-020 now bounds it to at most 5.5 s (TBR), below the 7.5 s floor of the hardware cutoff, package decision 36, OQ-SAF-005); power steps with a 1 W default (HZ-001 K1 and K2).
controls.note: REQ-SYS-020 reads at most 5.5 s (TBR) since 2026-09-25, consistent with REQ-SYS-055; the value closes with package decision 36 (OQ-SAF-005).

controls.text: The firmware stuck-key controls of HZ-004 (K3 manual-closure timeout, K4 no-gap paddle watchdog with squeeze limit) end an unintended key-down or key stream.

Reference antennas with an insulated base and tip (the Signal Stick's sheath), a counterpoise wire insulated along its length with a covered end; handbook: do not touch the antenna or the counterpoise while transmitting, extend a telescopic whip before keying.
The transmitter survives an open or shorted port for 60 s (HZ-009 K3), so removing the antenna while keyed damages nothing; the female SMA jack's recessed centre contact limits finger access.
The hardware PA-enable cutoff of HZ-004 K5 bounds any continuous carrier to 13 s; a toggling stream is bounded in hardware only by K6 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180).

The transmission-length backstop of HZ-004 K12 (REQ-SYS-180) ends antenna-port RF, independently of firmware, after 180 s (TBR) of continuous transmit, which bounds the time a toggling key stream keeps transmit voltage on the port and the antenna tip without operator intent. Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (package decision 38); if the owner declines, REQ-SYS-180 is retired by the SRR decision memo and this control becomes Dropped.

residual_risk.condition: Tune timeout and power defaults verified; reference antenna and counterpoise inspected for insulation.

hazards.fault_tolerance: Controlled by design margin and procedure; the consequence is bounded to first aid; a continuous carrier is bounded by the HZ-004 hardware cutoff and a toggling stream by firmware and, once package decision 38 adopts it, by the backstop K6 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180).

hazards.title: Sharp edges and pinch points of the machined enclosure
hazards.description: The enclosure is CNC-machined 6061 aluminum (bead blast plus Type II anodize) in two or more parts with a battery compartment, a display window, connector cutouts and two encoders with printed knobs. Machined edges and cutouts are sharp unless an edge break is specified (PCBWay machines to the model; ISO 2768-m says nothing about deburring); the lid-to-body joint, the battery compartment cover and the knob-to-bezel gap are pinch points; anodize chips and burrs at drilled holes cut skin.

causes.cause: No edge break or deburr callout on the drawing, so the vendor delivers sharp machined edges.
Knob-to-bezel clearance under 1 mm or a knob skirt overlapping the panel (pinch or skin catch when turning).
Battery compartment cover or lid with a lever action on closing (finger pinch).
Burrs at tapped holes and connector cutouts, anodize chipping at sharp corners, a broken antenna stub (HZ-009).

hazards.effects: Cuts and abrasions to the fingers (first aid), skin caught in a knob gap, a cut during battery replacement by a friend, cosmetic damage. Register safety dimension 3.
hazards.rationale: Severity Marginal: a first-aid cut. Likelihood B uncontrolled: an undeburred machined edge cuts the first user who handles it firmly, and the radio is handled daily in the hand and the pocket by several people (SI-019). Confidence High (PCBWay DFM and finish statements are High confidence in the enclosure report).

firmware_role.statement: None; a mechanical hazard with no firmware role.

controls.text: Every external edge and cutout edge broken by a chamfer or fillet of at least 0.5 mm modelled in OpenSCAD and called out on the drawing; internal pocket corners R2 minimum; drilled and tapped holes deburred (drawing note); bead blast finish before anodize.

tbr.plan: Confirmed against PCBWay's corner-radius and edge rules and the STEP export fidelity at PDR; recorded in the ME requirements and the drawing template.

controls.text: Knob-to-bezel radial clearance of at least 1.0 mm with the knob skirt not overlapping the panel; printed knob edges rounded; the encoder bushing length matched to the panel stack so the nut engages (R-UI-08).
Battery compartment cover and lid designed without a lever pinch (sliding or captive-screw cover), no exposed cell edges, cells accessible without tools sharper than a coin.

Printed (H2C) fit-check parts handled by the owner before the CNC order; receipt inspection of the machined parts for burrs and sharp edges with a finger-drag and a cotton-swab snag test; deburring by the owner before assembly if needed.
Battery replacement procedure in the handbook (radio off, cover handling, polarity).

residual_risk.condition: Edge breaks on the drawing and confirmed at receipt inspection of every machined part.

hazards.verification_note: K1 to K3: Inspection of the rendered enclosure model and the drawing callouts (PDR, CDR) and of the delivered parts (receipt inspection: cotton-swab snag test on every edge, gap gauge for knob clearance, cover closing trial); REQ-SYS-110 and REQ-SYS-111 close by the Analysis method accepted per RSK-018 with a scripted check on the STEP model (Simulation class) and the receipt Inspection as supporting evidence. K4: Inspection of the fit-check and receipt-inspection reports. K5: Inspection of the handbook.

hazards.title: Firmware load leaving the radio in an unsafe state
hazards.description: Firmware is loaded over the Pico 2 micro-USB through the RP2350 bootrom (BOOTSEL, UF2 or picotool). A corrupt, truncated, wrong-target or tampered image, an interrupted load, a configuration store left inconsistent (TX-arm state, power step, guest lock, frequency calibration, keyer mode, thermal threshold), or the undefined pad states during the bootloader and after reset could leave the PA enabled, the transmitter keyed, the frequency limits or protections inactive, or the power step at 5 W while the operator believes the protections are present.

causes.cause: A wrong or corrupt image flashed (a file from outside firmware/releases/, an interrupted USB transfer).
An image without a valid integrity trailer boots and drives outputs before any check.
Persisted configuration corrupted or out of range: a calibration offset that could move the carrier, power step 5 W, guest lock cleared, thermal threshold wrong.
TX_KEY and PA_EN pads undefined during the bootloader (reset: input-disabled, weak internal pull-down 36 to 113 kohm, no drive) or driven by a wrong pin map in a new image.

A new release changes the pin map or the defaults without the acceptance tests being re-run; a pin-map or PWM-slice error can drive TX_KEY (and PA_EN) with a periodic output (HZ-004 C10), which the retriggerable hardware cutoff does not bound.
Firmware version and hash not verified after flashing (VDD mismatch).

hazards.effects: Unintended emission at power-up (HZ-004), out-of-band emission from a wrong calibration (bounded to +/-370 Hz by the TCXO when calibration is zeroed), loss of the thermal, charging or audio protections while the operator believes them present (HZ-002, HZ-003, HZ-005), or a unit that starts at 5 W in a guest's hands (HZ-006).
hazards.rationale: Severity Critical: the worst credible outcome is a unit whose software protections are silently absent, routing to the Critical hazards HZ-004 and HZ-006. Likelihood B uncontrolled: flashing a wrong or interrupted image, or a release whose pin map or defaults changed without the acceptance cases being re-run, is a single operator or transfer error that the owner and friends will meet during the project (the owner and friends flash updates from the handbook), which is the B anchor of section 3.3; re-rated from C to B after independent review. Confidence High for the pad reset states (RP2350 datasheet) and the process controls (07 and 04 sections named in sources).

firmware_role.statement: A loaded image is itself a potential cause (criterion a); the boot path verifies the image integrity trailer and the configuration before any safety-critical output is enabled, initialises to the safe state (PA off, key up, charger in its hardware default, audio muted), replaces invalid configuration with safe defaults and reports the event (criteria c and e).
components: Safe-state manager (boot path, SW-BOOT, configuration guard)

controls.text: The image carries a CRC-32 trailer written by the release script and verified at boot before any safety-critical output is enabled; a failed check enters SafeState with a fault code and never enables the PA (SWE-134 a, f; coding standard CS-32).

Persisted configuration stored as two copies with CRC-32 and a sequence number; every safety-relevant field range-checked at load (power step, guest lock, calibration, thermal thresholds, keyer mode, debounce); out-of-range or corrupt values replaced by safe defaults (1 W step, 0.5 W tune, calibration zero, default thresholds) with a logged event and an LCD indication; both copies corrupt gives defaults (SWE-193 acceptance).

External 4.7 kohm pull-downs on TX_KEY and PA_EN so that bootloader, reset and isolated pad states read low at the PA logic; the T/R relay's unpowered state connects the antenna to the receiver; the hardware PA-enable cutoff and the charger and protector limits are independent of the image (HZ-004 K5, K6). The cutoff bounds a continuous key-down only; a periodic TX_KEY from a pin-map error is bounded in hardware only by K8 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180).

USB is present during every firmware load, so the hardware transmit inhibit on VBUS (HZ-011 K1, REQ-SYS-092) holds the PA off throughout the load and the bootloader; with the cells removed the PA also has no supply (HZ-011 K3, REQ-SYS-149).

Only tagged releases from firmware/releases/ with a version description (version, hash) are flashed; picotool verify after every flash; the boot banner reports version and hash; the TC-SW-BOOT and TC-SW-CFG acceptance cases (valid image accepted; corrupt, truncated and wrong-target images rejected with SafeState and a fault code; configuration defaults restored) run on the Bench at stage 4 of every unit's ATP as their SWE-193 credit run, with the logic behind them (CRC and range checks, default substitution) closed by HostUnit cases of REQ-SW-BOOT-* and REQ-SW-CFG-* and the non-USB parts run in Emulation as supporting ordering evidence only (credit: false) (SWE-193; 04 section 11.1); a release that changes the pin map re-runs the keying cases of the ATP.
After every reset the key-closed interlock (HZ-004 K1) re-runs, the CPU watchdog is enabled before transmit can be armed, and the reset reason is recorded (SWE-134 a).
RP2350 secure boot (signed images, irreversible OTP) evaluated in an ADR at PDR; not enabled in rev A unless the owner decides otherwise, because it cannot be undone (07 section 16).

The transmission-length backstop of HZ-004 K12 (REQ-SYS-180) ends antenna-port RF, independently of the loaded image, after 180 s (TBR) with the T/R drive in transmit, which bounds a periodic TX_KEY output from a release pin-map error (C5; hazard-analysis.md section 5, coverage row 8) that the K3 cutoff does not see; with it the PA-path gate is proposed to require the T/R transmit drive, so a periodic TX_KEY with T/R in receive gives no PA output (confirmed at PDR). Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR (package decision 38); if the owner declines, REQ-SYS-180 is retired by the SRR decision memo and this control becomes Dropped.

residual_risk.condition: An unsafe state after a load needs a bad image that passes the integrity check plus a hardware backstop failure for a continuous key-down (E). A release whose pin map drives TX_KEY and PA_EN with a periodic output and escapes the acceptance cases is ended by K8 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180, Proposed, package decision 38) after 180 s (TBR), so a sustained unsafe transmission also needs a backstop failure (E): Critical-E, Low, with every control that has a requirement verified. If the owner declines package decision 38, REQ-SYS-180 is retired, K8 becomes Dropped and the residual is Critical-D, Medium (the periodic output has no hardware bound; a process lapse plus an uncommon error), which section 3.4 accepts only with the listed controls allocated and verified and the owner's acceptance at SAR; the HZ-004 decline record applies to the same branch.

hazards.verification_note: K1, K2, K6: HostUnit (CRC and range-check logic, defaults; REQ-SW-BOOT-* and REQ-SW-CFG-* cases) as the closing Test (SWE-192); Emulation of the non-USB parts (corrupt image and corrupted configuration scenarios, boot-to-safe-state ordering) as supporting ordering evidence only (credit: false, ACC-EMU-001); Bench at stage 4 of the power-on sequence as the SWE-193 credit run of TC-SW-BOOT and TC-SW-CFG on every unit (SWE-134 a safe-state report, corrupt image rejected, defaults restored). K3, K4: Inspection of the schematic and Bench (PA_EN and TX_KEY low in bootloader mode; no RF with USB applied; no PA rail with USB only). K5: Inspection of the VDD, the release script and the ATP records. K7: Inspection of the ADR. K8: as HZ-004 K12.
single_point_failures: Release script writing the CRC trailer (a wrong trailer on a good image blocks the unit, which is fail-safe); the bootrom itself is Raspberry Pi's and outside the project's control
hazards.fault_tolerance: Single-fault tolerant for a continuous key-down (the pull-downs and the hardware cutoff are independent of the image) and during the load itself (hardware transmit inhibit on VBUS); single-fault tolerant for a periodic TX_KEY from a release pin-map error with K8 (HZ-004 K12, REQ-SYS-180), zero-fault tolerant in hardware for it if package decision 38 declines the backstop.

Package decision 38 (SRR): HZ-004 K12 transmission-length backstop (REQ-SYS-180), this hazard's K8, which bounds the pin-map stream case

hazards.title: Owner hand assembly: iron burns, flux fumes, solder handling, bench fire and heat or ESD damage to parts
hazards.description: The kit model (SI-031, ADR-007, REQ-SYS-137, REQ-SYS-138) has the owner hand-solder the through-hole parts and exposed-pad modules (Pico 2 castellations, 18650 holders, jacks, encoders, an RF module if one is chosen) onto boards on which PCBWay has placed the surface-mount parts, for at most five units (SI-035). The energy and agents: a soldering iron tip and barrel well above 300 C, molten solder and freshly soldered joints, rosin-based flux fume released at every joint, solder and flux residue on the hands, clipped leads and flux spatter, and the heat and electrostatic charge applied next to vendor-placed parts that are sensitive to both (the RP2350 module, the PA device, the LNA, the TCXO). The work is done at a home bench; the bench gear of CON-016 lists no soldering station, so the iron's features are an owner confirmation.

causes.cause: Contact with the iron tip or barrel, molten solder or a freshly soldered joint or part (grasping the barrel, catching a falling iron, touching a jack body just soldered).
Iron left energized off its stand or unattended, or placed near combustible material, igniting the bench.
Rosin flux fume inhaled at the joint with no extraction or ventilation; colophony fume is a respiratory irritant and sensitiser (general occupational-health knowledge, not a corpus source).
Solder and flux residue carried from the hands to the mouth (eating or drinking at the bench), or a leaded alloy used from old stock instead of the lead-free alloy of the assembly procedure.
A clipped lead or flux spatter thrown into the eye.

Excess heat or dwell on a castellated Pico 2 pad, a holder or jack terminal, lifting pads or damaging nearby vendor-placed parts; an ungrounded iron tip or an unearthed owner discharging into an ESD-sensitive part.
Soldering or rework with cells in the holders or USB connected, energising the board under the iron (routed to HZ-007 C8).

hazards.effects: Contact burn from the iron or a hot joint (first aid for a touch; a partial-thickness burn needing medical treatment if the barrel is grasped or the iron falls onto skin); a bench fire from an unattended iron, which is a fire not contained to the unit (Catastrophic on the section 3.2 scale); respiratory irritation from flux fume and, over a long build without extraction, sensitisation; an eye injury from a clipped lead or spatter; heat or ESD damage to a vendor-placed part, found at first power-on (SI-010) or latent, destroying the unit without fire at worst. Register safety dimension 5 for the fire case and 4 for a burn or eye injury needing treatment.
hazards.rationale: Severity Catastrophic because the worst credible outcome is a bench fire from an iron left energized off its stand, a fire not contained to the unit; the injury cases (a burn needing treatment, an eye injury) are Critical. Likelihood D in the uncontrolled state for the fire: one lapse (the iron left on and off its stand) plus an uncommon condition (combustible material in reach). The injury cases are more frequent: a touch burn is common (B) but first aid only, and the forms needing treatment need an uncommon action (Critical-C, Serious). Confidence Low for the fire likelihood (no fleet data; the owner's iron is not recorded), Medium for the injury cases. Added after independent review: SEMP section 7.1 lists the owner's hand soldering in the hazard scope and SI-031 makes the owner the assembler.

firmware_role.statement: None; an assembly hazard with no firmware role.

controls.text: Soldering station as equipment: temperature-controlled, with a stand, an auto-sleep or auto-off timer that lowers or removes tip heat when the iron is left idle, and an earthed, ESD-safe tip. It acts without the owner's attention, which is why it counts as the one control of the fire case that is neither software nor procedure (section 8.1 item 6). The owner confirms or obtains the station (package decision 100). Requirement pending (OQ-SAF-019). The practice of using it is K6.

Fume extraction at the joint (a fan with an activated-carbon filter drawing away from the face, or a window-vented extractor) in a ventilated room; no soldering with the face over the joint. Requirement pending (OQ-SAF-019).

Hand assembly limited by the part-category split of the release package to the through-hole parts and exposed-pad modules listed in the hand-assembly file, with every hidden-pad and fine-pitch part placed by PCBWay (SI-031, ADR-007), so no heat-sensitive fine-pitch rework is left to the owner.

residual_risk.condition: Only K3 is allocated; K1, K2, K4, K5 and K6 have no requirement yet (OQ-SAF-019), so the residual equals the uncontrolled fire case, Catastrophic-D, Serious. Section 3.4 position: this Serious residual does not meet the section 3.4 Serious terms and is not offered for acceptance at SRR. Those terms need at least two independent controls, one of them neither software nor procedure, each verified by Test; today the only allocated control, K3 (REQ-SYS-137, REQ-SYS-138), closes by Analysis and addresses heat and ESD damage to parts, not the bench fire that sets the severity. Path to PDR: the owner confirms the station of K1 (package decision 100); the requirements author writes the hand-assembly requirement for K1, K2, K4, K5 and K6 (OQ-SAF-019, due PDR); K1 is then verified by Test (the owner leaves the idle iron off its stand and times the tip temperature fall against the auto-sleep time the station datasheet states, read with the multimeter thermocouple if OQ-VV-003 confirms one, otherwise with the station's own temperature readout) and K4, K5, K6 by Inspection. With K1 and K6 allocated and verified, a bench fire needs the iron left on off its stand, the auto-sleep defeated or failed and combustible material in reach, so the residual becomes Catastrophic-E, Medium, accepted by the owner at SAR; the injury cases fall to Marginal (first aid). If the station has no auto-sleep, the residual stays Catastrophic-D, Serious, with one procedure barrier (K6), which section 3.4 does not accept; a hazard in that state at PDR is handled under the section 3.4 High and Serious responses.
